    79				Kind:            canonical.OpLLM,
    80				Name:            "message",
    81				Model:           m.model,
    82				Provider:        provider,
    83			},
    84			canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{
    85				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
    86				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
    87				TurnSeq:         turnSeq,
    88				Seq:             opSeq,
    89				Status:          "completed",
    90				EndTs:           tsUs,
    91			},
    92			m.payloadRef(advance(tsUs), turnSeq, opSeq, "llm_response", "json", bodyBytes),
    93		)
    94		if phaseFromRaw(rec.Raw) == "final_answer" {
    95			out = append(out, m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "INF", "final_answer", nil))
    96		}
    97		return out
    98	}
    99	
   100	// emitUserInput emits the internal user_input op pair + body PayloadRef, deduped
   101	// against the companion event_msg.user_message form (spec rule #6, #18). When
   102	// the fingerprint was already seen, it returns nil so the UI sees exactly one
   103	// user op per logical input. A user message also opens a new turn under the
   104	// active turn_id when none is open (old-CLI user-message boundary, spec edge #3).
   105	//
   106	// SOW-0089 chunk 5c — sub-turn splitting. When the active codex turn has
   107	// ALREADY seen a user_input op (count >= 1) AND has no in-flight tool call
   108	// awaiting its *_output, we finalize the current turn (synthetic
   109	// TurnFinalizedEvent, status=completed, end_ts=now) and open a new sub-turn
   110	// with synthetic codex_turn_id "sub:<counter>". The new sub-turn inherits
   111	// the parent's model/sandbox/effort/approval_policy (snapped from
   112	// turn_context — the codex format doesn't re-emit these per user_input).
   113	//
   114	// Skipping the split when hasOpenToolCall is true avoids orphaning a
   115	// function_call whose *_output is still pending — we'd produce two turns
   116	// with the tool call in the prior turn and its output in the new turn,
   117	// which the in-flight tracker (m.openOps) can't represent. The split
   118	// happens on the NEXT user_input after the tool resolves.
   119	func (m *fileMapper) emitUserInput(advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64, text, format string, bodyBytes int64) []canonical.Event {
   120		if !m.firstSeenUser(userFingerprint(text)) {
   121			return nil
   122		}
   123		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 4)
   124	
   125		// Sub-turn split: close the current turn (if it has user inputs already)
   126		// and open a new sub-turn. NO split if a tool call is in flight.
   127		if m.haveActiveTurn {
   128			if active, ok := m.turns[m.activeTurnID]; ok {
   129				if active.userInputCount >= 1 && !active.hasOpenToolCall && !active.finalized {
   130					out = append(out, m.finalizeTurnForSubSplit(advance, active, tsUs)...)
   131					// Open the new sub-turn with a synthetic codex_turn_id. openTurn
   132					// resets ts.userInputCount to 0 and ts.hasOpenToolCall to false via
   133					// the new turnState constructor. Per-turn policy snapshots (sandbox,
   134					// effort, approvalPolicy) carry over via the prior turn's
   135					// turnExtras, NOT via ts.model — the model/provider are owned by
   136					// fileMapper (file-level state, not per-turn).
   137					m.subTurnCounter++
   138					subID := fmt.Sprintf("sub:%d", m.subTurnCounter)
   139					subTs := m.openTurn(subID, tsUs)
   140					subTs.sandbox = active.sandbox
   141					subTs.effort = active.effort
   142					subTs.approvalPolicy = active.approvalPolicy
   143				}
   144			}
   145		}
   146	
   147		ts := m.ensureTurn(tsUs)
   148		if ev := m.emitTurnStarted(ts, advance(tsUs)); ev != nil {
   149			out = append(out, ev)
   150		}
   151		turnSeq, opSeq := m.nextOp(ts)
   152		ts.userInputCount++
   153		out = append(out,
   154			canonical.OpStartedEvent{
   155				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   156				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   157				TurnSeq:         turnSeq,
   158				Seq:             opSeq,
   159				ParentOpSeq:     -1,
   160				Kind:            canonical.OpInternal,
   161				Name:            "user_input",
   162			},
   163			canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{
   164				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   165				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   166				TurnSeq:         turnSeq,
   167				Seq:             opSeq,
   168				Status:          "completed",
   169				EndTs:           tsUs,
   170			},
   171			m.payloadRef(advance(tsUs), turnSeq, opSeq, "tool_request", format, bodyBytes),
   172		)
   173		return out
   174	}
   175	
   176	// mapReasoning handles response_item.reasoning (spec rule #8, acceptance #4). It
   177	// emits an OpReasoning pair with reasoning_kind = "summary" when only summary[]
   178	// is non-empty, "raw" when content[] carries text OR encrypted_content is set.
   179	// The body goes to a PayloadRef (Format=text for a summary, json for the full
   180	// item). event_msg.agent_reasoning* is a LogEntry only (ops_event.go) so the UI
   181	// never sees a duplicate reasoning op.
   182	func (m *fileMapper) mapReasoning(p *responseItemPayload, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs, bodyBytes int64) []canonical.Event {
   183		kind, format := reasoningKind(p)
   184		ts := m.ensureTurn(tsUs)
   185		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 4)
   186		if ev := m.emitTurnStarted(ts, advance(tsUs)); ev != nil {
   187			out = append(out, ev)
   188		}
   189		turnSeq, opSeq := m.nextOp(ts)
   190		out = append(out,
   191			canonical.OpStartedEvent{
   192				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   193				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   194				TurnSeq:         turnSeq,
   195				Seq:             opSeq,
   196				ParentOpSeq:     -1,
   197				Kind:            canonical.OpReasoning,
   198				Name:            "reasoning",
   199				ReasoningKind:   kind,
   200			},
   201			canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{
   202				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   203				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   204				TurnSeq:         turnSeq,
   205				Seq:             opSeq,
   206				Status:          "completed",
   207				EndTs:           tsUs,
   208			},
   209			m.payloadRef(advance(tsUs), turnSeq, opSeq, "llm_reasoning", format, bodyBytes),
   210		)
   211		return out
   212	}
   213	
   214	// reasoningKind classifies a reasoning item (spec rule #8, acceptance #4):
   215	// "summary" when only summary[] is non-empty (PayloadRef Format=text), "raw"
   216	// when content[] has text or encrypted_content is set (Format=json). When both
   217	// summary and raw signals are present, raw wins (the durable model state is the
   218	// fuller record). Defaults to "raw"/json when the item is opaque (encrypted).
   219	func reasoningKind(p *responseItemPayload) (kind, format string) {
   220		hasSummary := jsonArrayNonEmpty(p.Summary)
   221		hasContent := jsonArrayNonEmpty(p.Content)
   222		hasEnc := len(jsonTrim(p.EncryptedContent)) > 0
   223		switch {
   224		case hasContent || hasEnc:
   225			return "raw", "json"
   226		case hasSummary:
   227			return "summary", "text"
   228		default:
   229			// No discernible body (rare); treat as raw so the op is not mislabeled
   230			// a summary it does not carry.
   231			return "raw", "json"
   232		}
   233	}
   234	
   235	// jsonArrayNonEmpty reports whether raw is a JSON array with at least one
   236	// element. Tolerates null/absent (returns false).
   237	func jsonArrayNonEmpty(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
   238		body := jsonTrim(raw)
   239		if len(body) == 0 {
   240			return false
   241		}
   242		var arr []json.RawMessage
   243		if json.Unmarshal(body, &arr) != nil {
   244			return false
   245		}
   246		return len(arr) > 0
   247	}
   248	
   249	// messageText extracts the concatenated text of a message content[] array for
   250	// the user-dedup fingerprint (spec rule #6). Each element is
   251	// {type:"input_text"|"output_text"|..., text}. Returns "" when absent or when no
   252	// element carries text.
   253	func messageText(raw json.RawMessage) string {
   254		body := jsonTrim(raw)
   255		if len(body) == 0 {
   256			return ""
   257		}
   258		var items []struct {
   259			Text string `json:"text"`
   260		}
   261		if json.Unmarshal(body, &items) != nil {
   262			return ""
   263		}
   264		var b strings.Builder
   265		for _, it := range items {
   266			b.WriteString(it.Text)
   267		}
   268		return b.String()
   269	}
   270	
   271	// phaseFromRaw reads the optional message.phase ("commentary" | "final_answer")
   272	// off the verbatim payload bytes (spec rule #7). phase is a sibling field not
   273	// kept in the typed responseItemPayload, so it is decoded narrowly from the
   274	// payload object inside the envelope. Returns "" when absent or unparseable.
   275	func phaseFromRaw(raw []byte) string {
   276		var env struct {
   277			Payload struct {
   278				Phase string `json:"phase"`
   279			} `json:"payload"`
   280		}
   281		if json.Unmarshal(raw, &env) != nil {
   282			return ""
   283		}
   284		return env.Payload.Phase
   285	}
   286	
   287	// finalizeTurnForSubSplit (SOW-0089 chunk 5c) emits a synthetic
   288	// TurnFinalizedEvent for `ts` (the active codex turn) to close it BEFORE we
   289	// open a new sub-turn at a user_input boundary. The event carries:
   290	//
   291	//   - Status: "completed" (a sub-split is NOT a failure — the codex task
   292	//     itself is still alive; we're just visualizing one user/assistant
   293	//     exchange as its own turn).
   294	//   - EndTs: tsUs (the timestamp of the new user_input that triggered the
   295	//     split — operator sees an accurate duration for the prior sub-turn).
   296	//   - The full per-turn extras (rollup, sandbox, ttft_ms, etc) so the
   297	//     finalized sub-turn's row in turns.extras_json is complete.
   298	//
   299	// We mark ts.finalized=true so a subsequent task_complete (for the parent
   300	// codex task) does NOT re-finalize this turn (finalizeTurn is idempotent
   301	// on the flag — see mapper_turn.go).
   302	func (m *fileMapper) finalizeTurnForSubSplit(advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, ts *turnState, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
   303		if ts.finalized {
   304			return nil
   305		}
   306		base := advance(tsUs)
   307		return []canonical.Event{m.finalizeTurn(ts, base, tsUs, "completed", "")}
   308	}

    11	// finalizeAtEOF is the EOF-finalize surface the scanner (Chunk C) calls
    12	// UNCONDITIONALLY when a rollout file has been fully read to EOF (F1). The
    13	// behavior splits on the most-recent open turn's format and on staleness:
    14	//
    15	//   - OLD-format open turn (turn_context-only, no task_started — cli < ~0.93):
    16	//     finalize the turn COMPLETED, REGARDLESS of staleness (spec edge #3 "close
    17	//     at EOF"). Real corpus: 1,006 files (38%) are pure old-format ending cleanly
    18	//     with no completion marker — without this they would be mislabeled crashes.
    19	//     NO SessionFinalizedEvent (codex has no per-session terminal signal — SOW
    20	//     C#3); the session stays running and the UI uses last_activity_ts.
    21	//   - NEW-format open turn (saw a task_started but no task_complete/turn_aborted):
    22	//     finalize the turn FAILED/incomplete AND emit SessionFinalizedEvent(failed,
    23	//     incomplete) ONLY when `stale` (mtime ≥ 1 h — the scanner owns the check;
    24	//     spec rule #23, SOW C#3). On a FRESH new-format file the turn is left open
    25	//     (it is legitimately still running; the next append continues it).
    26	//   - No open turn (clean end, or never opened a turn): nothing — stays running.
    27	//
    28	// nowUs is the synthetic end timestamp (the scanner passes the file mtime in
    29	// micros). Idempotent: a second call is a no-op. The scanner now calls this at
    30	// EVERY full-read EOF (not only when stale) and passes the stale bool, so the
    31	// OLD-format completed-close fires on fresh files too (F1).
    32	func (m *fileMapper) finalizeAtEOF(stale bool, nowUs int64) []canonical.Event {
    33		if m.eofFinalized {
    34			return nil
    35		}
    36		ts := m.mostRecentOpenTurn()
    37		if ts == nil {
    38			// No open turn: the session ended cleanly (or never opened a turn).
    39			// Codex has no per-session terminal signal, so it stays running. Mark
    40			// finalized so a later call is a no-op.
    41			m.eofFinalized = true
    42			return nil
    43		}
    44		if !ts.sawTaskStarted {
    45			// OLD-format: close COMPLETED at EOF regardless of staleness (spec edge #3).
    46			// EndTs MUST be the turn's LAST-CONTENT-ACTIVITY timestamp (m.lastContentTsUs,
    47			// the max ts over content records — which, for the most-recent open turn, IS
    48			// that turn's last activity), NOT the file mtime / wall-clock (G6) and NOT
    49			// m.lastTsUs (which a metadata-only session_meta append would advance,
    50			// re-dating the close — I2). A clean old-format turn ended when its last real
    51			// record was written. Fall back to nowUs only when no content record carried a
    52			// timestamp (lastContentTsUs == 0).
    53			endUs := m.lastContentTsUs
    54			if endUs == 0 {
    55				endUs = nowUs
    56			}
    57			m.eofFinalized = true
    58			return m.closeOpenTurnAtEOF(ts, endUs, "completed", "", false)
    59		}
    60		// NEW-format: only a stale file's hanging turn is a crash (rule #23). A fresh
    61		// file's turn is still running — leave it open (do NOT set eofFinalized, so a
    62		// later stale sweep can still close it).
    63		if !stale {
    64			return nil
    65		}
    66		m.eofFinalized = true
    67		return m.closeOpenTurnAtEOF(ts, nowUs, "failed", "incomplete", true)
    68	}
    69	
    70	// closeOpenTurnAtEOF finalizes a hanging turn at EOF: its dangling ops are closed
    71	// (cancelled for a crashed new-format turn, completed for a cleanly-ended
    72	// old-format turn), the turn is finalized with the supplied status/errClass, its
    73	// turn-extras log is emitted, and — only when withSessionFinalize is set (the
    74	// stale new-format crash path) — a SessionFinalizedEvent(failed, incomplete) is
    75	// appended (the ONLY SessionFinalizedEvent codex emits; SOW C#3). closeUs is the
    76	// close timestamp: the turn's last-activity ts for the OLD-format completed close
    77	// (deterministic, G6) or the file mtime for the stale new-format crash close. It
    78	// is floored at the turn's start so the synthetic close never predates the open.
    79	func (m *fileMapper) closeOpenTurnAtEOF(ts *turnState, closeUs int64, status, errClass string, withSessionFinalize bool) []canonical.Event {
    80		endUs := closeUs
    81		if endUs < ts.startTsUs {
    82			endUs = ts.startTsUs
    83		}
    84		base := func() canonical.EventBase {
    85			return canonical.EventBase{SourceID: m.sourceID, SourceSeq: 0, Ts: endUs}
    86		}
    87		danglingStatus := "cancelled"
    88		if status == "completed" {
    89			// An old-format turn that ended cleanly: its in-flight ops (e.g. a final
    90			// assistant message with no explicit output) are treated as completed, not
    91			// cancelled — the session did not crash.
    92			danglingStatus = "completed"
    93		}
    94		out := m.finalizeDanglingOps(ts.codexTurnID, base, endUs, danglingStatus)
    95		out = append(out, m.finalizeTurn(ts, base(), endUs, status, errClass))
    96		if withSessionFinalize {
    97			out = append(out, canonical.SessionFinalizedEvent{
    98				EventBase:  base(),
    99				NativeID:   m.nativeID,
   100				Status:     canonical.StatusFailed,
   101				ErrorClass: "incomplete",
   102				EndTs:      endUs,
   103			})
   104		}
   105		return out
   106	}
   107	
   108	// mostRecentOpenTurn returns the latest-opened turn that has not been finalized,
   109	// or nil when every turn is closed (or none exist). Used by finalizeAtEOF and
   110	// the replaced/superseded-turn helpers.
   111	func (m *fileMapper) mostRecentOpenTurn() *turnState {
   112		for i := len(m.turnOrder) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
   113			if ts, ok := m.turns[m.turnOrder[i]]; ok && !ts.finalized {
   114				return ts
   115			}
   116		}
   117		return nil
   118	}

   120	// packSeq packs (recordIdx, subIdx) into a single uint64 that is monotone per
   121	// file. subIdx is masked to subEventBits. Mirrors claude_code.
   122	func packSeq(recordIdx, subIdx uint64) uint64 {
   123		return recordIdx<<subEventBits | (subIdx & (maxSubEventsPerRecord - 1))
   124	}

   126	// parseTsToMicros decodes an RFC3339 timestamp into UNIX microseconds. Codex
   127	// writes UTC RFC3339 with millisecond precision (spec adapter-codex.md:56);
   128	// nano precision is accepted too.
   129	func parseTsToMicros(s string) (int64, error) {
   130		t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, s)
   131		if err != nil {
   132			return 0, fmt.Errorf("ts %q: %w", s, err)
   133		}
   134		return t.UnixMicro(), nil
   135	}

   137	// trimPreview returns at most maxRunes runes of s with surrounding whitespace
   138	// removed, for a non-sensitive Extras preview (e.g. compaction message,
   139	// last_agent_message). Bodies are never inlined wholesale — full content lives
   140	// behind the PayloadRef (spec edge #7).
   141	func trimPreview(s string, maxRunes int) string {
   142		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
   143		if maxRunes <= 0 {
   144			return ""
   145		}
   146		r := []rune(s)
   147		if len(r) <= maxRunes {
   148			return s
   149		}
   150		return string(r[:maxRunes])
   151	}

    85			// thread_goal_updated, guardian_assessment, view_image_tool_call,
    86			// dynamic_tool_call_*, and any future persisted variant: keep visible.
    87			return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "DBG", "event_msg:"+p.Type, nil)}, nil
    88		}
    89	}
    90	
    91	// mapTaskStarted handles event_msg.task_started (alias turn_started) (spec rule
    92	// #3, #22). It opens the turn for turn_id (idempotent with turn_context) and
    93	// emits TurnStartedEvent the first time. started_at (unix seconds) is used as
    94	// the canonical Ts when it is newer than the wire timestamp. model_context_window
    95	// is stashed for the turn's LLM ctx_max (spec rule #3, #17).
    96	func (m *fileMapper) mapTaskStarted(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
    97		p := rec.EventMsg
    98		startUs := tsUs
    99		if sa := startedAtMicros(rec.Raw); sa > startUs {
   100			startUs = sa
   101		}
   102		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 4)
   103		// A new turn_id opening supersedes the prior open turn (F1/F2, spec edge #2/#3).
   104		// In a new-format session task_started follows turn_context, so the prior turn
   105		// is usually already superseded by the turn_context handler; this call covers
   106		// the task_started-first ordering and is a no-op for the same turn_id. The
   107		// prior turn's close status is decided by ITS OWN format inside the helper.
   108		out = append(out, m.supersedePriorTurn(p.TurnID, advance, startUs)...)
   109		ts := m.openTurn(p.TurnID, startUs)
   110		ts.sawTaskStarted = true
   111		if ev := m.emitTurnStarted(ts, advance(startUs)); ev != nil {
   112			out = append(out, ev)
   113		}
   114		if mcw := modelContextWindow(rec.Raw); mcw > 0 {
   115			ts.ctxMax = mcw
   116		}
   117		return out
   118	}
   119	
   120	// mapTaskComplete handles event_msg.task_complete (alias turn_complete) (spec
   121	// rule #4). It finalizes the turn (completed) with the C#1 token rollup,
   122	// finalizes every dangling op tied to the turn (status "completed" inferred —
   123	// codex output for a completed turn that lacked an explicit _output is treated
   124	// as success), records ttft_ms, and applies the turn's accumulated CtxUsed/CtxMax
   125	// to its last LLM op (spec rule #4, #17). completed_at is the EndTs when present.
   126	func (m *fileMapper) mapTaskComplete(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
   127		p := rec.EventMsg
   128		ts, ok := m.turns[p.TurnID]
   129		if !ok {
   130			// task_complete with no open turn: surface and skip so a stray
   131			// completion does not double-close (spec edge robustness).
   132			return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "WRN", "task_complete_no_turn", map[string]any{"turn_id": p.TurnID})}
   133		}
   134		// SOW-0089 chunk 5c — sub-turn routing. When chunk 5c splits a codex task
   135		// into N sub-turns at user_input boundaries, the original turn (the one
   136		// keyed by the codex turn_id, here "t1") is finalized synthetically at
   137		// the LAST user_input. The final sub-turn ("sub:<n>") remains active and
   138		// holds the LAST user_input + the LAST assistant reply. When
   139		// task_complete arrives with the ORIGINAL turn_id, we route the close
   140		// to the LAST still-open turn (which is the most-recent sub-turn, not
   141		// the original "t1" — which is already finalized).
   142		target := ts
   143		if ts.finalized {
   144			if last := m.mostRecentOpenTurn(); last != nil {
   145				target = last
   146			} else {
   147				// No open sub-turn to finalize — surface and skip (the original
   148				// turn was already finalized by a sub-split and nothing came after).
   149				return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "WRN", "task_complete_no_turn", map[string]any{"turn_id": p.TurnID})}
   150			}
   151		}
   152		endUs := tsUs
   153		if ca := completedAtMicros(rec.Raw); ca > 0 {
   154			endUs = ca
   155		}
   156		if ttft := ttftMillis(rec.Raw); ttft > 0 {
   157			target.ttftMs = ttft
   158		}
   159		base := func() canonical.EventBase { return advance(endUs) }
   160		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 4)
   161		// Apply the accumulated ctx to the turn's last LLM op (spec rule #17).
   162		if ev, ok := m.applyLLMCtx(target, base); ok {
   163			out = append(out, ev)
   164		}
   165		// Finalize dangling ops BEFORE the turn close so they share the turn (spec
   166		// rule #4, edge #9: status completed inferred at task_complete).
   167		out = append(out, m.finalizeDanglingOps(target.codexTurnID, base, endUs, "completed")...)
   168		out = append(out, m.finalizeTurn(target, base(), endUs, "completed", ""))
   169		return out
   170	}
   171	
   172	// mapTurnAborted handles event_msg.turn_aborted (spec rule #5, edge #2). It
   173	// finalizes the turn (failed) with the reason→ErrorClass mapping and finalizes
   174	// dangling ops as "cancelled" (edge #9 — the user interrupted, so in-flight ops
   175	// did not complete). completed_at is the EndTs when present.
   176	func (m *fileMapper) mapTurnAborted(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
   177		p := rec.EventMsg
   178		ts, ok := m.turns[p.TurnID]
   179		if !ok || ts.finalized {
   180			return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "WRN", "turn_aborted_no_turn", map[string]any{"turn_id": p.TurnID})}
   181		}
   182		endUs := tsUs
   183		if ca := completedAtMicros(rec.Raw); ca > 0 {
   184			endUs = ca
   185		}
   186		base := func() canonical.EventBase { return advance(endUs) }
   187		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 3)
   188		out = append(out, m.finalizeDanglingOps(p.TurnID, base, endUs, "cancelled")...)
   189		out = append(out, m.finalizeTurn(ts, base(), endUs, "failed", abortErrorClass(p.Reason)))
   190		return out
   191	}

   193	// mapTokenCount handles event_msg.token_count (spec rule #17, C#1). It folds the
   194	// per-call last_token_usage into the attributed turn's rollup and stashes the
   195	// cumulative total / model_context_window for the turn's last LLM op. A
   196	// token_count carrying turn_id attributes to that turn; one without attributes
   197	// to the most-recently-active turn ("Token accounting nuance"). model_context_
   198	// window is also surfaced to the catalog via the next LLM op's CtxMax at turn
   199	// finalize. token_count itself emits no event.
   200	func (m *fileMapper) mapTokenCount(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
   201		p := rec.EventMsg
   202		info := decodeTokenCount(rec.Raw)
   203		ts := m.tokenTurn(p.TurnID)
   204		if ts == nil {
   205			// No turn to attribute to yet (token_count before any turn opened):
   206			// surface a DBG log so it is visible — never drop silently (spec rule #6
   207			// "no silent failures"; F6). The counts cannot be attributed (rare and
   208			// not load-bearing), but the drop is recorded with the offending turn_id.
   209			return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "DBG", "token_count_no_turn", map[string]any{"turn_id": p.TurnID})}
   210		}
   211		ts.addTokenUsage(info)
   212		return nil
   213	}
   214	
   215	// tokenTurn resolves the turn a token_count attributes to (spec rule #17,
   216	// "Token accounting nuance"): the turn for turn_id when present and known, else
   217	// the most-recently-active turn. Returns nil when no turn is open.
   218	func (m *fileMapper) tokenTurn(turnID string) *turnState {
   219		if turnID != "" {
   220			if ts, ok := m.turns[turnID]; ok {
   221				return ts
   222			}
   223		}
   224		if m.haveActiveTurn {
   225			if ts, ok := m.turns[m.activeTurnID]; ok {
   226				return ts
   227			}
   228		}
   229		return nil
   230	}
   231	
   232	// applyLLMCtx emits an OpFinalizedEvent that sets CtxUsed/CtxMax AND the turn's
   233	// accumulated token/cost totals on the turn's last LLM op (spec rule #17, C#1,
   234	// SOW-0030). The ingester rolls session/turn token totals FROM OP rows, so
   235	// codex tokens must land on an op — putting them on TurnFinalizedEvent only
   236	// (as before) meant they never persisted (the aggregate model ignores
   237	// TurnFinalized token fields). The turn's last LLM op is the natural attribution
   238	// point: it is the op that consumed the tokens. The ingester reconciles this
   239	// finalize with the op's earlier finalize (idempotent upsert keyed on
   240	// (turn,seq)). Returns (event, true) when emitted, (zero, false) when there is
   241	// nothing to apply.
   242	func (m *fileMapper) applyLLMCtx(ts *turnState, base func() canonical.EventBase) (canonical.OpFinalizedEvent, bool) {
   243		if ts.lastLLMOpSeq == 0 || (ts.lastLLMCtxUsed == 0 && ts.ctxMax == 0 && ts.tokensIn == 0 && ts.tokensOut == 0) {
   244			return canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{}, false
   245		}
   246		endUs := ts.lastLLMEndTs
   247		if endUs == 0 {
   248			endUs = ts.startTsUs
   249		}
   250		return canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{
   251			EventBase:        base(),
   252			SessionNativeID:  m.nativeID,
   253			TurnSeq:          ts.seq,
   254			Seq:              ts.lastLLMOpSeq,
   255			Status:           "completed",
   256			EndTs:            endUs,
   257			CtxUsed:          ts.lastLLMCtxUsed,
   258			CtxMax:           ts.ctxMax,
   259			TokensIn:         ts.tokensIn,
   260			TokensOut:        ts.tokensOut,
   261			TokensCacheRead:  ts.tokensCacheRead,
   262			TokensCacheWrite: ts.tokensCacheWrite,
   263		}, true
   264	}

   266	// stashAgentMessage records event_msg.agent_message.message as the active
   267	// turn's last_agent_message preview (spec rule #19). Truncated to previewMax
   268	// runes; full text lives in the response_item.message PayloadRef.
   269	func (m *fileMapper) stashAgentMessage(msg string) {
   270		if !m.haveActiveTurn {
   271			return
   272		}

   274			if prev := trimPreview(msg, previewMax); prev != "" {
   275				ts.lastAgentMessage = prev

   277		}

   280	// abortErrorClass maps a turn_aborted reason to a canonical ErrorClass (spec
   281	// rule #5). Unknown reasons pass through verbatim (forward-compat).
   282	func abortErrorClass(reason string) string {
   283		switch reason {
   284		case "interrupted":
   285			return "user_interrupt"
   286		case "replaced":
   287			return "replaced"
   288		case "review_ended":
   289			return "review_ended"
   290		case "budget_limited":
   291			return "rate_limit"
   292		default:
   293			return reason
   294		}
   295	}

   298	// time — codex_turn_id, sandbox, effort, approval_policy, ttft_ms,
   299	// last_agent_message (spec "Canonical Model Gaps" #2, #3, #8; rule #19). It is
   300	// attached to TurnFinalizedEvent.Extras, which the ingest writer marshals into
   301	// turns.extras_json (SOW-0021). Returns nil when the turn carried no surfaced
   302	// metadata (so the writer writes NULL, not "{}").
   303	func (m *fileMapper) turnExtras(ts *turnState) map[string]any {
   304		extras := map[string]any{}
   305		if ts.codexTurnID != "" {
   306			extras["codex_turn_id"] = ts.codexTurnID
   307		}
   308		if ts.sandbox != "" {
   309			extras["sandbox"] = ts.sandbox
   310		}
   311		if ts.effort != "" {
   312			extras["effort"] = ts.effort
   313		}
   314		if ts.approvalPolicy != "" {
   315			extras["approval_policy"] = ts.approvalPolicy
   316		}
   317		if ts.ttftMs > 0 {
   318			extras["ttft_ms"] = ts.ttftMs
   319		}
   320		if ts.lastAgentMessage != "" {
   321			extras["last_agent_message"] = ts.lastAgentMessage
   322		}
   323		if len(extras) == 0 {
   324			return nil
   325		}

   327	}

   337	// startedAtMicros reads task_started.started_at (unix seconds) from the raw
   338	// payload and returns it in micros, or 0 when absent (spec rule #3).
   339	func startedAtMicros(raw []byte) int64 {
   340		v := payloadNumber(raw, "started_at")
   341		if v == 0 {
   342			return 0
   343		}
   344		return v * 1_000_000
   345	}
   346	
   347	// completedAtMicros reads task_complete/turn_aborted.completed_at, accepting
   348	// either an RFC3339 string or a unix-seconds number, and returns micros (0 when
   349	// absent). codex versions vary in the encoding (spec rule #4, #5).
   350	func completedAtMicros(raw []byte) int64 {
   351		var env struct {
   352			Payload struct {
   353				CompletedAt json.RawMessage `json:"completed_at"`
   354			} `json:"payload"`
   355		}
   356		if json.Unmarshal(raw, &env) != nil {
   357			return 0
   358		}
   359		body := jsonTrim(env.Payload.CompletedAt)
   360		if len(body) == 0 {
   361			return 0
   362		}
   363		var s string
   364		if json.Unmarshal(body, &s) == nil {
   365			if us, err := parseTsToMicros(s); err == nil {
   366				return us
   367			}
   368			return 0
   369		}
   370		var secs int64
   371		if json.Unmarshal(body, &secs) == nil {
   372			return secs * 1_000_000
   373		}
   374		return 0
   375	}
   376	
   377	// ttftMillis reads task_complete.time_to_first_token_ms (spec gap #8).
   378	func ttftMillis(raw []byte) int64 { return payloadNumber(raw, "time_to_first_token_ms") }

     5	// enrichOp merges telemetry from an event_msg end-event onto the op matched by
     6	// call_id, so the enrichment Extras reach the op's ops.extras_json (F4, spec rule
     7	// #14 exec_command_end). The merge is ORDER-INDEPENDENT — real exec ordering is
     8	// exec_command_end BEFORE function_call_output in ~68-85% of files and after it
     9	// in the rest:
    10	//   - op still OPEN (exec-first, the common case): merge the extras onto the
    11	//     tracked op and stash any exec-derived terminal status; the op STAYS OPEN so
    12	//     its *_output finalizes it (mapToolOutput re-emits an OpStarted carrying the
    13	//     merged Extras at that point — OpFinalizedEvent has no Extras field, and the
    14	//     writer upserts (turn,seq), so the re-emit is an idempotent UPDATE, not a
    15	//     second op, satisfying rule #14 "do not emit a second op"). If no *_output
    16	//     ever arrives, the turn-close dangling finalize re-emits the Extras.
    17	//   - op already FINALIZED (output-first): look it up in finalizedOps and emit an
    18	//     OpStarted carrying the merged Extras to UPDATE the existing row.
    19	//   - op NOT locatable (start below a resume offset, or orphaned): a DBG log is
    20	//     the only honest surface (no op row to attach to).
    21	//
    22	// extractor builds the Extras map from the raw payload (nil → no extras, e.g.
    23	// image_generation_end which only marks completion). A blanked-output
    24	// exec_command_end (Limited mode clears stdout/stderr) is NOT an error — the
    25	// status stays the op's derived terminal status (spec rule #14).
    26	func (m *fileMapper) enrichOp(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64, extractor func([]byte) map[string]any) []canonical.Event {
    27		p := rec.EventMsg
    28		var extras map[string]any
    29		if extractor != nil {
    30			extras = extractor(rec.Raw)
    31		}
    32		status, errClass := enrichStatus(rec.Raw)
    33	
    34		op, ok := m.openOps[p.CallID]
    35		if !ok {
    36			// The op may have already been finalized by its *_output before this
    37			// end-event (the ~15-32% output-first ordering): re-emit an OpStarted onto
    38			// the finalized op so the Extras land AND, when the exec carries an explicit
    39			// exit_code, a CORRECTING OpFinalized so a non-zero exit overrides the
    40			// output-derived status (G1, spec rule #5/#14 — exit_code is authoritative
    41			// in BOTH orders).
    42			return m.enrichFinalizedOp(p.CallID, advance, tsUs, p.Type, extras, status, errClass)
    43		}
    44		// Op still open (exec-first): stash extras + the exec-derived status on the op
    45		// and leave it open. Its *_output (or the turn-close dangling finalize) emits
    46		// the canonical OpFinalized AND re-emits an OpStarted carrying these Extras. The
    47		// exec status WINS over the output-string heuristic when exec carries an
    48		// explicit exit_code (spec rule #5/#14).
    49		mergeExtras(op, extras)
    50		if status != "" {
    51			op.enrichStatus = status
    52			op.enrichErrClass = errClass
    53		}
    54		return nil
    55	}
    56	
    57	// enrichFinalizedOp handles an end-event whose op was already finalized by its
    58	// *_output (output-first ordering, ~15-32% of exec files) (F4/G1). It re-emits an
    59	// OpStarted carrying the enrichment Extras to UPDATE the existing op row
    60	// (idempotent on (turn,seq) — NOT a second op) AND, when the end-event carries an
    61	// authoritative terminal status (an exec exit_code — spec rule #5/#14), a
    62	// CORRECTING OpFinalized so a failed exec that was provisionally finalized
    63	// completed by its output string is upserted to failed/command_failed (G1). When
    64	// the op cannot be located in finalizedOps (start below a resume offset, or
    65	// orphaned), a DBG log is the only honest surface.
    66	func (m *fileMapper) enrichFinalizedOp(callID string, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64, evType string, extras map[string]any, status, errClass string) []canonical.Event {
    67		fop, ok := m.finalizedOps[callID]
    68		if !ok {
    69			log := map[string]any{"call_id": callID}
    70			for k, v := range extras {
    71				log[k] = v
    72			}
    73			return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "DBG", "enrich_"+evType, log)}
    74		}
    75		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 2)
    76		if len(extras) > 0 {
    77			out = append(out, m.reemitOpStarted(fop, advance, tsUs, extras))
    78		}
    79		// An explicit exit_code-derived status corrects the op's terminal status in the
    80		// output-first ordering: the *_output already finalized it (often completed off a
    81		// benign-looking output), but a non-zero exit_code is authoritative (G1, spec
    82		// rule #5/#14). The writer upserts on (turn,seq), so this overwrites the status.
    83		//
    84		// Emit the correcting OpFinalized ONLY when the enrichment-derived status differs
    85		// from the one the op was already finalized with (H1b). An exec exit 0 on an
    86		// already-`completed` op carries no correction, so re-emitting OpFinalized(completed)
    87		// would be spurious — and the catalog rollups (which contribute each finalize's
    88		// failure/token/duration totals) would double-count it. A genuine change
    89		// (completed → failed on a non-zero exit) still corrects exactly once.
    90		if status != "" && (status != fop.status || errClass != fop.errClass) {
    91			out = append(out, m.correctFinalizedOp(fop, advance, tsUs, status, errClass))
    92		}
    93		if len(out) == 0 {
    94			return nil
    95		}
    96		return out
    97	}

    99	// correctFinalizedOp emits an OpFinalized that re-applies an authoritative
   100	// terminal status onto an already-finalized op's (turn,seq) row (G1). Used when an
   101	// exec_command_end exit_code (output-first ordering) must override the status the
   102	// op's *_output provisionally set. The writer's ON CONFLICT upsert overwrites the
   103	// status/errClass on the existing row; EndTs is the enrichment event's timestamp.
   104	func (m *fileMapper) correctFinalizedOp(fop finalizedOp, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64, status, errClass string) canonical.Event {
   105		return canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{
   106			EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   107			SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   108			TurnSeq:         fop.turnSeq,
   109			Seq:             fop.opSeq,
   110			Status:          status,
   111			ErrorClass:      errClass,
   112			EndTs:           tsUs,
   113		}
   114	}

   149	// reemitOpStarted builds an idempotent OpStarted that carries enrichment Extras
   150	// onto an already-finalized op's (turn,seq) row (F4). The writer's ON CONFLICT
   151	// UPDATE merges the Extras and keeps the original start_ts (MIN) and status
   152	// (the finalize already set it), so this only adds the late telemetry.
   153	func (m *fileMapper) reemitOpStarted(fop finalizedOp, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64, extras map[string]any) canonical.Event {
   154		return canonical.OpStartedEvent{
   155			EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   156			SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   157			TurnSeq:         fop.turnSeq,
   158			Seq:             fop.opSeq,
   159			ParentOpSeq:     -1,
   160			Kind:            fop.kind,
   161			Name:            fop.name,
   162			ToolNamespace:   fop.namespace,
   163			Extras:          extras,
   164		}
   165	}
   166	
   167	// recordFinalizedOp records a now-finalized op so a LATE enrichment event can
   168	// merge Extras onto it via reemitOpStarted (F4). The op's kind/name/namespace are
   169	// preserved so the re-emit restates the op faithfully. status/errClass are the
   170	// TERMINAL status the op was finalized with, so an output-first enrichment only
   171	// emits a correcting OpFinalized when its authoritative status actually differs
   172	// from this one (H1b — no spurious re-finalize on an unchanged status).
   173	func (m *fileMapper) recordFinalizedOp(callID string, op *openOp, status, errClass string) {
   174		if callID == "" {
   175			return
   176		}
   177		m.finalizedOps[callID] = finalizedOp{
   178			turnSeq:   op.turnSeq,
   179			opSeq:     op.opSeq,
   180			kind:      op.kind,
   181			name:      op.name,
   182			namespace: op.namespace,
   183			status:    status,
   184			errClass:  errClass,
   185		}
   186	}
   187	
   188	// refreshHasOpenToolCall (SOW-0089 chunk 5c) recomputes ts.hasOpenToolCall from
   189	// the live openOps map. Called when a tool call finalizes (its output
   190	// arrived) so subsequent user_input events can decide whether to split a
   191	// sub-turn. We don't store a per-turn count — openOps is keyed by call_id
   192	// globally, so we have to filter by ts.codexTurnID on each refresh. Cheap
   193	// (openOps has at most a handful of entries at any time).
   194	func (m *fileMapper) refreshHasOpenToolCall(turnID string) {
   195		ts, ok := m.turns[turnID]
   196		if !ok {
   197			return
   198		}
   199		hasOpen := false
   200		for _, op := range m.openOps {
   201			if op.turnID == turnID {
   202				hasOpen = true
   203				break
   204			}
   205		}
   206		ts.hasOpenToolCall = hasOpen
   207	}
   208	
   209	// enrichWebSearch handles event_msg.web_search_end (F7/G4, spec rule #11). It
   210	// pairs POSITIONALLY with the OLDEST open web_search op (the FRONT of the
   211	// openWebSearch FIFO queue), because web_search_call carries no correlation key;
   212	// FIFO order means interleaved searches pair in the order they opened. It
   213	// finalizes that op completed and re-emits an OpStarted carrying the query +
   214	// action Extras (OpFinalized has no Extras field). When no web_search is open
   215	// (the end is orphaned, or its call was below a resume offset), a DBG log keeps it
   216	// visible.
   217	func (m *fileMapper) enrichWebSearch(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
   218		ws := m.dequeueWebSearch()
   219		if ws == nil {
   220			return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "DBG", "web_search_end_no_call", nil)}
   221		}
   222		extras := webSearchExtras(rec.Raw)
   223		op, ok := m.openOps[ws.syntheticCallID]
   224		if !ok {
   225			// The op was already finalized (e.g. at a prior turn close) — re-emit onto
   226			// its row via the positional ref.
   227			fop := finalizedOp{turnSeq: ws.turnSeq, opSeq: ws.opSeq, kind: canonical.OpTool, name: "web_search", namespace: "web"}
   228			if len(extras) == 0 {
   229				return nil
   230			}
   231			return []canonical.Event{m.reemitOpStarted(fop, advance, tsUs, extras)}
   232		}
   233		op.finalized = true
   234		mergeExtras(op, extras)
   235		delete(m.openOps, ws.syntheticCallID)
   236		m.recordFinalizedOp(ws.syntheticCallID, op, "completed", "")
   237		return m.finalizeWithExtras(op, advance, tsUs, "completed", "")
   238	}
   239	
   240	// dequeueWebSearch pops the OLDEST open web_search op (front of the FIFO queue)
   241	// for positional pairing with a web_search_end (G4). Returns nil when the queue is
   242	// empty (an orphaned end). Skips refs whose op already finalized at a turn close
   243	// (its synthetic call_id is gone from openOps) so a stale front entry never
   244	// shadows a still-open later search.
   245	func (m *fileMapper) dequeueWebSearch() *openWebSearchRef {
   246		for len(m.openWebSearch) > 0 {
   247			ws := m.openWebSearch[0]
   248			m.openWebSearch = m.openWebSearch[1:]
   249			if _, stillOpen := m.openOps[ws.syntheticCallID]; stillOpen {
   250				return ws
   251			}
   252			// The op was finalized at a prior turn close; its query/action can no longer
   253			// be paired meaningfully — keep scanning for a still-open search. (Pairing a
   254			// closed op would just re-stamp Extras; the FIFO contract is to pair the
   255			// oldest STILL-OPEN search, so we drop the closed ref and continue.)
   256		}
   257		return nil
   258	}
   259	
   260	// enrichMcp handles event_msg.mcp_tool_call_end (spec rule #15). It re-stamps
   261	// the matching op's ToolNamespace to "mcp:<server>" and Name to the invocation
   262	// tool by emitting an OpStarted update (the ingester upserts on (turn,seq), so a
   263	// second OpStarted with the corrected namespace/name overwrites the placeholder
   264	// from the function_call), then finalizes the op with the result status. When no
   265	// op matches, it surfaces a DBG log.
   266	func (m *fileMapper) enrichMcp(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
   267		p := rec.EventMsg
   268		server, tool := mcpInvocation(rec.Raw)
   269		op, ok := m.openOps[p.CallID]
   270		if !ok {
   271			extras := map[string]any{"call_id": p.CallID}
   272			if server != "" {
   273				extras["server"] = server
   274			}
   275			if tool != "" {
   276				extras["tool"] = tool
   277			}
   278			return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "DBG", "enrich_mcp_tool_call_end", extras)}
   279		}
   280		name := op.name
   281		if tool != "" {
   282			name = tool
   283		}
   284		namespace := "custom"
   285		if server != "" {
   286			namespace = "mcp:" + server
   287		}
   288		op.name = name
   289		op.namespace = namespace
   290		status, errClass := mcpResultStatus(rec.Raw)
   291		op.finalized = true
   292		out := []canonical.Event{
   293			canonical.OpStartedEvent{
   294				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   295				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   296				TurnSeq:         op.turnSeq,
   297				Seq:             op.opSeq,
   298				ParentOpSeq:     -1,
   299				Kind:            canonical.OpTool,
   300				Name:            name,
   301				ToolNamespace:   namespace,
   302			},
   303			canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{
   304				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   305				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   306				TurnSeq:         op.turnSeq,
   307				Seq:             op.opSeq,
   308				Status:          status,
   309				ErrorClass:      errClass,
   310				EndTs:           tsUs,
   311			},
   312		}
   313		delete(m.openOps, p.CallID)
   314		m.recordFinalizedOp(p.CallID, op, status, errClass)
   315		return out
   316	}
   317	
   318	// enrichPatchApply handles event_msg.patch_apply_end (spec rule #16,
   319	// adapter-codex.md:361). It is ORDER-INDEPENDENT (G2), mirroring the exec fix:
   320	//   - op still OPEN (the apply_patch function_call_output has not arrived):
   321	//     finalize the op with the success/status-derived terminal status and merge
   322	//     {patch_success, patch_status} into its Extras via an OpStarted re-emit.
   323	//   - op already FINALIZED (output-first): re-emit an OpStarted carrying the
   324	//     extras AND a correcting OpFinalized so success=false upserts the op to
   325	//     failed/patch_failed (spec rule #16 "Set Op Status accordingly").
   326	//   - op NOT locatable: a DBG log is the only honest surface.
   327	func (m *fileMapper) enrichPatchApply(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
   328		p := rec.EventMsg
   329		status, errClass := patchApplyStatus(rec.Raw)
   330		extras := patchApplyExtras(rec.Raw)
   331		op, ok := m.openOps[p.CallID]
   332		if !ok {
   333			// Output-first ordering: the op was already finalized by its
   334			// function_call_output — merge the extras and correct the status on its row.
   335			return m.enrichFinalizedOp(p.CallID, advance, tsUs, p.Type, extras, status, errClass)
   336		}
   337		op.finalized = true
   338		mergeExtras(op, extras)
   339		delete(m.openOps, p.CallID)
   340		m.recordFinalizedOp(p.CallID, op, status, errClass)
   341		// finalizeWithExtras emits the OpStarted (carrying patch_success/patch_status)
   342		// followed by the OpFinalized with the success-derived status.
   343		return m.finalizeWithExtras(op, advance, tsUs, status, errClass)
   344	}
   345	
   346	// mergeExtras folds enrichment extras onto a tracked op so its eventual finalize
   347	// (if not produced here) carries them. A nil op or nil extras is a no-op.
   348	func mergeExtras(op *openOp, extras map[string]any) {
   349		if op == nil || len(extras) == 0 {
   350			return
   351		}
   352		if op.extras == nil {
   353			op.extras = map[string]any{}
   354		}
   355		for k, v := range extras {
   356			op.extras[k] = v
   357		}
   358	}

    90	// Scan implements canonical.Adapter. Walks the sessions root, reads each modern
    91	// rollout from its cursor offset to EOF, and emits canonical events. Returns
    92	// when caught up or when ctx is cancelled. The caller owns `out`; Scan never
    93	// closes it. Mirrors claude_code.Scan: the final offsets are recorded on the
    94	// instance even on cancellation so a following Tail resumes from completed work.
    95	func (a *Adapter) Scan(ctx context.Context, since canonical.Cursor, out chan<- canonical.Event) error {
    96		start := a.coerceCursor(since)
    97		final, sErr := scanAll(ctx, a.root, a.sourceID, start, out, a.onError)
    98		// Record the final offsets even on cancellation so a Tail that follows a
    99		// context-cancelled Scan still resumes from the work that was completed (the
   100		// cursor reflects only fully-consumed lines). On a hard error the cursor is
   101		// still the best resume point we have.
   102		cursorCopy := final
   103		a.scanCursor = &cursorCopy
   104		if sErr != nil {
   105			if errors.Is(sErr, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(sErr, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
   106				return nil
   107			}
   108			return fmt.Errorf("codex: scan: %w", sErr)
   109		}
   110		return nil
   111	}
   112	
   113	// Tail implements canonical.Adapter. Subscribes to fsnotify events on the
   114	// sessions tree and emits canonical events as rollouts grow. Returns when ctx is
   115	// cancelled. Same channel-ownership and cancellation rules as Scan. Tail resumes
   116	// from the per-file offsets the preceding Scan recorded on this instance,
   117	// closing the data-loss window where records appended BETWEEN Scan finishing and
   118	// Tail starting would be skipped if Tail snapshotted current EOF. Any re-emission
   119	// of an already-seen line is absorbed by the ingester's SQL-layer idempotent
   120	// upserts. A cold Tail with no preceding Scan falls back to current file sizes so
   121	// it follows from now rather than replaying full history. Mirrors
   122	// claude_code.Tail.
   123	func (a *Adapter) Tail(ctx context.Context, out chan<- canonical.Event) error {
   124		var cur Cursor
   125		if a.scanCursor != nil {
   126			cur = a.coerceCursor(*a.scanCursor)
   127		} else {
   128			snap, err := a.snapshotCursor()
   129			if err != nil {
   130				return fmt.Errorf("codex: tail snapshot: %w", err)
   131			}
   132			cur = snap
   133		}
   134		return tailLoop(ctx, a.root, a.sourceID, cur, out, a.onError)
   135	}

   196		}

   198	}

    70		kind canonical.SessionKind
    71		// agentName seeds SessionStartedEvent.AgentName (sub-agent: agent_nickname
    72		// or agent_role; else "codex:" + originator) (spec rule #1).
    73		agentName string

    75		// PayloadRef LocationURI ("file://<abs>#L<line>") for inline bodies that
    76		// live in the jsonl (user/assistant messages, reasoning, tool I/O,

    78		// tests; the URI then carries the line anchor without an absolute prefix.
    79		absPath string

    81		// symlink containment when building a PayloadRef LocationURI (security.md
    82		// §6, spec edge #7). Empty in mapper-only unit tests; payloadURI then skips
    83		// the containment resolve and emits the cleaned absolute path so URIs are
    84		// still anchored. The scanner sets it to the already-resolved root it opened
    85		// the file under (mirrors claude_code/mapper.go's root field).
    86		root string
    87	
    88		// lineNo is the 1-based file line number of the record currently being
    89		// mapped. The scanner (Chunk C) sets it via setLineNo before each mapRecord
    90		// so the PayloadRef LocationURI can anchor "#L<line>" at the owning record
    91		// (spec rule #6/#7/#8, edge #7 — large bodies are referenced, never
    92		// inlined). 0 disables the anchor (mapper-only tests that do not set it).
    93		lineNo int
    94	
    95		// recordIdx is the 0-based ordinal of the record being mapped, used to
    96		// derive a stable per-file SourceSeq. Monotone within a streaming pass.
    97		recordIdx uint64

    99		// sessionStarted guards the once-per-file SessionStartedEvent (spec rule #1).
   100		sessionStarted bool
   101		// modelSeen records that a SessionUpdatedEvent(Model) has been emitted, so
   102		// the model is announced exactly once when first learned from a turn_context
   103		// (spec rule #2).
   104		modelSeen bool
   105		// model is the active turn's model (latest turn_context.model). Stamped onto
   106		// every LLM/reasoning op so cost can be computed downstream (spec rule #2,
   107		// #7). Empty until the first turn_context carrying a model.
   108		model string
   109	
   110		// turns maps a codex turn_id (UUID) to the synthesized 1-based turn state.
   111		// A turn_id of "" is the absent-turn_id fallback bucket (old CLI without
   112		// turn_id — spec edge #3); it shares the same map under the empty key.
   113		turns map[string]*turnState
   114		// turnOrder lists turn_ids in open order so finalizeAtEOF / the
   115		// replaced/superseded-turn helpers can find the most recent still-open turn
   116		// deterministically (spec rule #23, edge #2/#3).
   117		turnOrder []string

   119		turnSeqCounter int

   121		// sub-turn opened when a new user_input arrives mid-codex-task. Used to
   122		// build the synthetic codex_turn_id "sub:<n>". Monotone per file.
   123		subTurnCounter int
   124		// activeTurnID is the turn_id of the most-recently-opened turn, used to
   125		// attribute a session-level token_count (no turn_id) to the right turn
   126		// (spec rule #17, "Token accounting nuance") and to drive the absent-turn_id
   127		// fallback (spec edge #3).
   128		activeTurnID string
   129		// haveActiveTurn distinguishes activeTurnID=="" "no turn yet" from
   130		// activeTurnID=="" "the absent-turn_id fallback turn is active".
   131		haveActiveTurn bool
   132	
   133		// openOps maps an in-flight tool/llm op's call_id to where it was emitted so
   134		// the matching *_output (or enrichment event) finalizes/enriches the same
   135		// op (spec rule #9, #14, #15, #16). A call_id of "" is never tracked.
   136		openOps map[string]*openOp
   137	
   138		// finalizedOps maps a finalized op's call_id to where it was emitted so a
   139		// LATE enrichment event (exec_command_end / patch_apply_end arriving AFTER the
   140		// op's *_output already finalized it) can still merge its Extras onto the op
   141		// via an idempotent OpStarted re-emit (F4, spec rule #14). Real exec ordering
   142		// is exec_command_end BEFORE function_call_output in ~68-85% of files but the
   143		// other ~15-32% put it after — the enrichment must reach the op in BOTH
   144		// orders. Entries persist for the life of the file (small; one per tool op).
   145		finalizedOps map[string]finalizedOp
   146	
   147		// openWebSearch is a FIFO QUEUE of not-yet-paired web_search ops, in open order
   148		// (F7/G4). web_search_call carries NEITHER id NOR call_id, so its companion
   149		// event_msg.web_search_end (which DOES carry call_id) cannot pair by key — it
   150		// pairs POSITIONALLY: each web_search_end finalizes the OLDEST open web_search op
   151		// (front of the queue), so interleaved searches pair in order and none are left
   152		// dangling out of sequence. Entries are appended on web_search_call, removed on
   153		// pairing (front) or when their turn closes (finalizeDanglingOps closes the op
   154		// and pruneClosedWebSearch drops the stale ref).
   155		openWebSearch []*openWebSearchRef
   156	
   157		// seenUserCallIDs dedups user input across response_item.message(role=user)
   158		// and event_msg.user_message (spec rule #6, #18). Keyed on a content
   159		// fingerprint so the second arrival is suppressed regardless of order.
   160		seenUser map[string]struct{}
   161	
   162		// eofFinalized guards finalizeAtEOF so the EOF-finalize is emitted at most
   163		// once per file even if the scanner calls it more than once. It is set only
   164		// when a terminal decision is made (an OLD-format turn closed completed, a
   165		// stale NEW-format turn closed failed, or no open turn); a FRESH new-format
   166		// file with an open turn does NOT set it, so a later stale sweep can still
   167		// close that turn (F1).
   168		eofFinalized bool
   169	
   170		// compactedSeen reports whether any top-level `compacted` line has emitted a
   171		// compaction op (F5), and compactedRecordIdx is the recordIdx of the most
   172		// recent such line. The real wire shape is a data-bearing top-level `compacted`
   173		// line IMMEDIATELY followed by a bare event_msg.context_compacted marker with
   174		// the SAME timestamp — two representations of ONE compaction. The op is emitted
   175		// from `compacted`; the adjacent context_compacted is suppressed (no second op)
   176		// when it is the very next record. A context_compacted with no preceding
   177		// compacted (defensive) emits the op itself (spec rule #20).
   178		compactedSeen      bool
   179		compactedRecordIdx uint64
   180	
   181		// lastTsUs is the timestamp (micros) of the most recent record carrying one,
   182		// across ALL record types (including a metadata-only session_meta append).
   183		// Observability only (cursor LastTsUs). Stays 0 for a file whose records all
   184		// lack timestamps.
   185		lastTsUs int64
   186	
   187		// lastContentTsUs is the timestamp (micros) of the most recent CONTENT-bearing
   188		// record — every record the mapper acts on EXCEPT a no-op session_meta (the
   189		// once-per-file bootstrap line, and any later metadata-only session_meta append
   190		// codex writes per recorder.rs:1615). It is the deterministic close-ts for an
   191		// OLD-format turn finalized at EOF (I2/G6): a metadata append grows the file and
   192		// advances lastTsUs, but the OLD-format turn ended when its LAST real record was
   193		// written — using lastContentTsUs keeps that close-ts stable across a
   194		// metadata-only append. Stays 0 until the first content record carrying a ts.
   195		lastContentTsUs int64
   196	}
   197	
   198	// The per-file inference STATE TYPES (turnState, openOp, finalizedOp,
   199	// openWebSearchRef) live in mapper_state.go.
   200	
   201	// mapperConfig bundles the per-file inputs newFileMapper needs.
   202	type mapperConfig struct {
   203		sourceID       string
   204		absPath        string
   205		nativeID       string
   206		parentNativeID string
   207		kind           canonical.SessionKind
   208		agentName      string
   209		// root is the symlink-resolved sessions root for PayloadRef containment
   210		// (security.md §6). Empty in mapper-only tests (no containment resolve).
   211		root string
   212	}
   213	
   214	// newFileMapper constructs a mapper for one rollout file.
   215	func newFileMapper(cfg mapperConfig) *fileMapper {
   216		return &fileMapper{
   217			sourceID:       cfg.sourceID,
   218			absPath:        cfg.absPath,
   219			root:           cfg.root,
   220			nativeID:       cfg.nativeID,
   221			parentNativeID: cfg.parentNativeID,
   222			kind:           cfg.kind,
   223			agentName:      cfg.agentName,
   224			turns:          map[string]*turnState{},
   225			openOps:        map[string]*openOp{},
   226			finalizedOps:   map[string]finalizedOp{},
   227			seenUser:       map[string]struct{}{},
   228		}
   229	}
   230	
   231	// setLineNo records the 1-based file line number of the next record the scanner
   232	// will feed to mapRecord, so a PayloadRef can anchor "#L<line>" at the owning
   233	// record (spec rule #6/#7/#8). The scanner (Chunk C) calls this before each
   234	// mapRecord; mapper-only unit tests may set it directly or leave it 0.
   235	func (m *fileMapper) setLineNo(n int) { m.lineNo = n }
   236	
   237	// mapRecord converts one parsed record into canonical events, advancing the
   238	// mapper's inference state. Pure with respect to I/O; mutates only the
   239	// receiver. The first call on any file emits the SessionStartedEvent (spec
   240	// rule #1). Records that produce nothing actionable (e.g. an event_msg the
   241	// adapter only uses for enrichment) return an empty slice.
   242	func (m *fileMapper) mapRecord(rec record) ([]canonical.Event, error) {
   243		idx := m.recordIdx
   244		m.recordIdx++
   245		if ts := m.recordTs(rec); ts > m.lastTsUs {
   246			m.lastTsUs = ts
   247		}
   248	
   249		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 4)
   250		sub := uint64(0)
   251		advance := func(tsUs int64) canonical.EventBase {
   252			b := canonical.EventBase{
   253				SourceID:  m.sourceID,
   254				SourceSeq: packSeq(idx, sub),
   255				Ts:        tsUs,
   256			}
   257			sub++
   258			return b
   259		}
   260	
   261		// Bootstrap the session on the first record (spec rule #1). session_meta is
   262		// always line 1, but the bootstrap keys on sessionStarted (not on the record
   263		// type) so a corrupt file missing session_meta still anchors its events to a
   264		// session row (the scanner surfaces the missing-meta SourceError per rule
   265		// #24 before any mapping).
   266		if !m.sessionStarted {
   267			out = append(out, m.sessionStarted0(rec, advance))
   268			m.sessionStarted = true
   269		}
   270	
   271		// A session_meta is the once-per-file bootstrap line, or a later metadata-only
   272		// append (recorder.rs:1615); it carries no turn content, so it must NOT advance
   273		// the OLD-format EOF close-ts (lastContentTsUs). Every other record type is
   274		// turn content and advances it (I2). recordTs returns 0 for a record with no
   275		// timestamp, which never moves the max.
   276		if rec.Type() != recSessionMeta {
   277			if ts := m.recordTs(rec); ts > m.lastContentTsUs {
   278				m.lastContentTsUs = ts
   279			}
   280		}
   281	
   282		switch rec.Type() {
   283		case recSessionMeta:
   284			// SessionStarted already emitted by the bootstrap above; a session_meta
   285			// arriving later (metadata-only append, recorder.rs:1610) carries no new
   286			// turn/op data the mapper acts on.
   287		case recTurnContext:
   288			out = append(out, m.mapTurnContext(rec, advance)...)
   289		case recResponseItem:
   290			evs, err := m.mapResponseItem(rec, advance)
   291			if err != nil {
   292				return nil, err
   293			}
   294			out = append(out, evs...)
   295		case recEventMsg:
   296			evs, err := m.mapEventMsg(rec, advance)
   297			if err != nil {
   298				return nil, err
   299			}
   300			out = append(out, evs...)
   301		case recCompacted:
   302			out = append(out, m.mapCompacted(rec, advance)...)
   303		default:
   304			// Unreachable: parseLine refuses unknown top-level types and skips
   305			// known no-op nested types before mapRecord is reached.
   306			return nil, fmt.Errorf("codex: unhandled record type %q", rec.Type())
   307		}
   308		return out, nil
   309	}
   310	
   311	// sessionStarted0 builds the once-per-file SessionStartedEvent (spec rule #1).
   312	// Kind, parent linkage, AgentName, and Extras (cli_version, originator, source,
   313	// cwd, git, sandbox, relationship) come from the session_meta payload when the
   314	// first record IS a session_meta (the normal case); a non-meta first record
   315	// (corrupt file) yields a minimal root session so its events still attach.
   316	func (m *fileMapper) sessionStarted0(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase) canonical.SessionStartedEvent {
   317		base := advance(m.recordTs(rec))
   318		ev := canonical.SessionStartedEvent{
   319			EventBase:      base,
   320			NativeID:       m.nativeID,
   321			RootNativeID:   m.rootNativeID(),
   322			ParentNativeID: m.parentNativeID,
   323			Kind:           m.kind,
   324			AgentName:      m.agentName,
   325		}
   326		if rec.SessionMeta != nil {
   327			applySessionMeta(&ev, rec.SessionMeta, m)
   328		} else if ev.Kind == "" {
   329			// Bootstrap fallback for a corrupt file whose first record is not a
   330			// session_meta (rule #24): a minimal root session so events still attach.
   331			// The scanner surfaces the missing-meta SourceError separately.
   332			ev.Kind = canonical.KindRoot
   333			m.kind = canonical.KindRoot
   334		}
   335		return ev
   336	}
   337	
   338	// rootNativeID returns the root of this session's tree. A child (fork or
   339	// sub-agent) points at its parent so the ingester resolver has a meaningful
   340	// root pointer even before the parent file lands (mirrors claude_code); a root
   341	// session is its own root (spec rule #1, "Sub-Agent Linkage").
   342	func (m *fileMapper) rootNativeID() string {
   343		if m.parentNativeID != "" {
   344			return m.parentNativeID
   345		}
   346		return m.nativeID
   347	}
   348	
   349	// recordTs parses the record's envelope timestamp to micros, or returns 0 when
   350	// the record lacks one. The envelope timestamp is the canonical time source
   351	// (spec adapter-codex.md:56-60).
   352	func (m *fileMapper) recordTs(rec record) int64 {
   353		if rec.Timestamp() == "" {
   354			return 0
   355		}
   356		us, err := parseTsToMicros(rec.Timestamp())
   357		if err != nil {
   358			return 0
   359		}
   360		return us

    75	pub(crate) fn build_wait_agent_statuses(
    76	    statuses: &HashMap<ThreadId, AgentStatus>,
    77	    receiver_agents: &[CollabAgentRef],
    78	) -> Vec<CollabAgentStatusEntry> {
    79	    if statuses.is_empty() {
    80	        return Vec::new();
    81	    }
    82	
    83	    let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(statuses.len());
    84	    let mut seen = HashMap::with_capacity(receiver_agents.len());
    85	    for receiver_agent in receiver_agents {
    86	        seen.insert(receiver_agent.thread_id, ());
    87	        if let Some(status) = statuses.get(&receiver_agent.thread_id) {
    88	            entries.push(CollabAgentStatusEntry {
    89	                thread_id: receiver_agent.thread_id,
    90	                agent_nickname: receiver_agent.agent_nickname.clone(),
    91	                agent_role: receiver_agent.agent_role.clone(),
    92	                status: status.clone(),
    93	            });
    94	        }
    95	    }
    96	
    97	    let mut extras = statuses
    98	        .iter()
    99	        .filter(|(thread_id, _)| !seen.contains_key(thread_id))
   100	        .map(|(thread_id, status)| CollabAgentStatusEntry {
   101	            thread_id: *thread_id,
   102	            agent_nickname: None,
   103	            agent_role: None,
   104	            status: status.clone(),
   105	        })
   106	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
   107	    extras.sort_by_key(|entry| entry.thread_id.to_string());
   108	    entries.extend(extras);
   109	    entries
   110	}

   112	pub(crate) fn collab_spawn_error(err: CodexErr) -> FunctionCallError {
   113	    match err {
   114	        CodexErr::UnsupportedOperation(message) if message == "thread manager dropped" => {
   115	            FunctionCallError::RespondToModel("collab manager unavailable".to_string())
   116	        }
   117	        CodexErr::UnsupportedOperation(message) => FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(message),
   118	        err => FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(format!("collab spawn failed: {err}")),
   119	    }
   120	}

   122	pub(crate) fn collab_agent_error(agent_id: ThreadId, err: CodexErr) -> FunctionCallError {
   123	    match err {
   124	        CodexErr::ThreadNotFound(id) => {
   125	            FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(format!("agent with id {id} not found"))
   126	        }
   127	        CodexErr::InternalAgentDied => {
   128	            FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(format!("agent with id {agent_id} is closed"))
   129	        }
   130	        CodexErr::UnsupportedOperation(_) => {
   131	            FunctionCallError::RespondToModel("collab manager unavailable".to_string())
   132	        }
   133	        err => FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(format!("collab tool failed: {err}")),
   134	    }
   135	}

   137	pub(crate) fn thread_spawn_source(
   138	    parent_thread_id: ThreadId,
   139	    parent_session_source: &SessionSource,
   140	    depth: i32,
   141	    agent_role: Option<&str>,
   142	    task_name: Option<String>,
   143	) -> Result<SessionSource, FunctionCallError> {
   144	    let agent_path = task_name
   145	        .as_deref()
   146	        .map(|task_name| {
   147	            parent_session_source
   148	                .get_agent_path()
   149	                .unwrap_or_else(AgentPath::root)
   150	                .join(task_name)
   151	                .map_err(FunctionCallError::RespondToModel)
   152	        })
   153	        .transpose()?;
   154	    Ok(SessionSource::SubAgent(SubAgentSource::ThreadSpawn {
   155	        parent_thread_id,
   156	        depth,
   157	        agent_path,
   158	        agent_nickname: None,
   159	        agent_role: agent_role.map(str::to_string),
   160	    }))
   161	}

   163	pub(crate) fn parse_collab_input(
   164	    message: Option<String>,
   165	    items: Option<Vec<UserInput>>,
   166	) -> Result<Op, FunctionCallError> {
   167	    match (message, items) {
   168	        (Some(_), Some(_)) => Err(FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(
   169	            "Provide either message or items, but not both".to_string(),
   170	        )),
   171	        (None, None) => Err(FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(
   172	            "Provide one of: message or items".to_string(),
   173	        )),
   174	        (Some(message), None) => {
   175	            if message.trim().is_empty() {
   176	                return Err(FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(
   177	                    "Empty message can't be sent to an agent".to_string(),
   178	                ));
   179	            }
   180	            Ok(vec![UserInput::Text {
   181	                text: message,
   182	                text_elements: Vec::new(),
   183	            }]
   184	            .into())
   185	        }
   186	        (None, Some(items)) => {
   187	            if items.is_empty() {
   188	                return Err(FunctionCallError::RespondToModel(
   189	                    "Items can't be empty".to_string(),
   190	                ));
   191	            }
   192	            Ok(items.into())
   193	        }
   194	    }
   195	}

   197	/// Builds the base config snapshot for a newly spawned sub-agent.
   198	///
   199	/// The returned config starts from the parent's effective config and then refreshes the
   200	/// runtime-owned fields carried on `turn`, including model selection, reasoning settings,
   201	/// approval policy, sandbox, and cwd. Role-specific overrides are layered after this step;
   202	/// skipping this helper and cloning stale config state directly can send the child agent out with
   203	/// the wrong provider or runtime policy.
   204	pub(crate) fn build_agent_spawn_config(
   205	    base_instructions: &BaseInstructions,
   206	    turn: &TurnContext,
   207	) -> Result<Config, FunctionCallError> {
   208	    let mut config = build_agent_shared_config(turn)?;
   209	    config.base_instructions = Some(base_instructions.text.clone());
   210	    Ok(config)
   211	}
   212	
   213	pub(crate) fn build_agent_resume_config(turn: &TurnContext) -> Result<Config, FunctionCallError> {
   214	    let mut config = build_agent_shared_config(turn)?;
   215	    // For resume, keep base instructions sourced from rollout/session metadata.
   216	    config.base_instructions = None;
   217	    Ok(config)
   218	}
   219	
   220	fn build_agent_shared_config(turn: &TurnContext) -> Result<Config, FunctionCallError> {
   221	    let base_config = turn.config.clone();
   222	    let mut config = (*base_config).clone();
   223	    config.model = Some(turn.model_info.slug.clone());
   224	    config.model_provider = turn.provider.info().clone();
   225	    config.model_reasoning_effort = turn
   226	        .reasoning_effort
   227	        .clone()
   228	        .or_else(|| turn.model_info.default_reasoning_level.clone());
   229	    config.model_reasoning_summary = Some(turn.reasoning_summary);
   230	    config.developer_instructions = turn.developer_instructions.clone();
   231	    apply_spawn_agent_runtime_overrides(&mut config, turn)?;
   232	
   233	    Ok(config)
   234	}

    31	/// Controls the per-command sandbox override requested by a shell-like tool call.
    32	#[derive(
    33	    Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, Eq, Hash, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema, TS,
    34	)]
    35	#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
    36	pub enum SandboxPermissions {
    37	    /// Run with the turn's configured sandbox policy unchanged.
    38	    #[default]
    39	    UseDefault,
    40	    /// Request to run outside the sandbox.
    41	    RequireEscalated,
    42	    /// Request to stay in the sandbox while widening permissions for this

    44	    WithAdditionalPermissions,
    45	}

    47	impl SandboxPermissions {
    48	    /// True if SandboxPermissions requires full unsandboxed execution (i.e. RequireEscalated)
    49	    pub fn requires_escalated_permissions(self) -> bool {
    50	        matches!(self, SandboxPermissions::RequireEscalated)
    51	    }
    52	
    53	    /// True if SandboxPermissions requests any explicit per-command override
    54	    /// beyond `UseDefault`.
    55	    pub fn requests_sandbox_override(self) -> bool {
    56	        !matches!(self, SandboxPermissions::UseDefault)
    57	    }
    58	
    59	    /// True if SandboxPermissions uses the sandboxed per-command permission
    60	    /// widening flow.
    61	    pub fn uses_additional_permissions(self) -> bool {
    62	        matches!(self, SandboxPermissions::WithAdditionalPermissions)
    63	    }
    64	}

   108	
   109	pub type LegacyReadWriteRoots<PathType = AbsolutePathBuf> =
   110	    (Option<Vec<PathType>>, Option<Vec<PathType>>);
   111	impl<PathType> FileSystemPermissions<PathType> {
   112	    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
   113	        self.entries.is_empty()
   114	    }
   115	
   116	    pub fn from_read_write_roots(
   117	        read: Option<Vec<PathType>>,
   118	        write: Option<Vec<PathType>>,
   119	    ) -> Self {
   120	        let mut entries = Vec::new();
   121	        if let Some(read) = read {
   122	            entries.extend(read.into_iter().map(|path| FileSystemSandboxEntry {
   123	                path: FileSystemPath::Path { path },
   124	                access: FileSystemAccessMode::Read,
   125	            }));
   126	        }
   127	        if let Some(write) = write {
   128	            entries.extend(write.into_iter().map(|path| FileSystemSandboxEntry {
   129	                path: FileSystemPath::Path { path },
   130	                access: FileSystemAccessMode::Write,
   131	            }));
   132	        }
   133	        Self {
   134	            entries,
   135	            glob_scan_max_depth: None,
   136	        }
   137	    }
   138	
   139	    pub fn explicit_path_entries(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&PathType, FileSystemAccessMode)> {
   140	        self.entries.iter().filter_map(|entry| match &entry.path {
   141	            FileSystemPath::Path { path } => Some((path, entry.access)),
   142	            FileSystemPath::GlobPattern { .. } | FileSystemPath::Special { .. } => None,
   143	        })
   144	    }
   145	
   146	    pub fn legacy_read_write_roots(&self) -> Option<LegacyReadWriteRoots<PathType>>
   147	    where
   148	        PathType: Clone,
   149	    {
   150	        self.as_legacy_permissions()
   151	            .map(|legacy| (legacy.read, legacy.write))
   152	    }
   153	
   154	    fn as_legacy_permissions(&self) -> Option<LegacyFileSystemPermissions<PathType>>
   155	    where
   156	        PathType: Clone,
   157	    {
   158	        if self.glob_scan_max_depth.is_some() {
   159	            return None;
   160	        }
   161	
   162	        let mut read = Vec::new();
   163	        let mut write = Vec::new();
   164	
   165	        for entry in &self.entries {
   166	            let FileSystemPath::Path { path } = &entry.path else {
   167	                return None;
   168	            };
   169	            match entry.access {
   170	                FileSystemAccessMode::Read => read.push(path.clone()),
   171	                FileSystemAccessMode::Write => write.push(path.clone()),
   172	                FileSystemAccessMode::Deny => return None,
   173	            }
   174	        }
   175	
   176	        Some(LegacyFileSystemPermissions {
   177	            read: (!read.is_empty()).then_some(read),
   178	            write: (!write.is_empty()).then_some(write),
   179	        })
   180	    }
   181	}
   182	
   183	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Eq, Hash, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   184	#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
   185	#[serde(bound(deserialize = "PathType: Deserialize<'de>"))]
   186	struct LegacyFileSystemPermissions<PathType = AbsolutePathBuf> {
   187	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   188	    read: Option<Vec<PathType>>,
   189	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   190	    write: Option<Vec<PathType>>,
   191	}
   192	
   193	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Eq, Hash, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
   194	#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
   195	#[serde(bound(deserialize = "PathType: Deserialize<'de>"))]
   196	struct CanonicalFileSystemPermissions<PathType = AbsolutePathBuf> {
   197	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
   198	    entries: Vec<FileSystemSandboxEntry<PathType>>,
   199	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
   200	    glob_scan_max_depth: Option<NonZeroUsize>,
   201	}
   202	
   203	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
   204	#[serde(untagged)]
   205	enum FileSystemPermissionsDe<PathType = AbsolutePathBuf> {
   206	    Canonical(CanonicalFileSystemPermissions<PathType>),
   207	    Legacy(LegacyFileSystemPermissions<PathType>),
   208	}
   209	
   210	impl<PathType> Serialize for FileSystemPermissions<PathType>
   211	where
   212	    PathType: Clone + Serialize,
   213	{
   214	    fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
   215	    where
   216	        S: Serializer,
   217	    {
   218	        if let Some(legacy) = self.as_legacy_permissions() {
   219	            legacy.serialize(serializer)
   220	        } else {
   221	            CanonicalFileSystemPermissions {
   222	                entries: self.entries.clone(),
   223	                glob_scan_max_depth: self.glob_scan_max_depth,
   224	            }
   225	            .serialize(serializer)
   226	        }
   227	    }
   228	}
   229	
   230	impl<'de, PathType> Deserialize<'de> for FileSystemPermissions<PathType>
   231	where
   232	    PathType: Deserialize<'de>,
   233	{
   234	    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
   235	    where
   236	        D: Deserializer<'de>,
   237	    {
   238	        match FileSystemPermissionsDe::deserialize(deserializer)? {
   239	            FileSystemPermissionsDe::Canonical(CanonicalFileSystemPermissions {
   240	                entries,
   241	                glob_scan_max_depth,
   242	            }) => Ok(Self {
   243	                entries,
   244	                glob_scan_max_depth,
   245	            }),
   246	            FileSystemPermissionsDe::Legacy(LegacyFileSystemPermissions { read, write }) => {
   247	                Ok(Self::from_read_write_roots(read, write))
   248	            }
   249	        }
   250	    }
   251	}

   320	impl From<ManagedFileSystemPermissions<AbsolutePathBuf>> for ManagedFileSystemPermissions<PathUri> {
   321	    fn from(value: ManagedFileSystemPermissions<AbsolutePathBuf>) -> Self {
   322	        match value {
   323	            ManagedFileSystemPermissions::Restricted {

   329	                    .map(FileSystemSandboxEntry::<PathUri>::from)
   330	                    .collect(),
   331	                glob_scan_max_depth,
   332	            },
   333	            ManagedFileSystemPermissions::Unrestricted => {
   334	                ManagedFileSystemPermissions::Unrestricted
   335	            }
   336	        }
   337	    }
   338	}

   355	                glob_scan_max_depth,
