  2727	impl SessionSource {
  2728	    pub fn from_startup_arg(value: &str) -> Result<Self, &'static str> {
  2729	        let trimmed = value.trim();
  2730	        if trimmed.is_empty() {
  2731	            return Err("session source must not be empty");
  2732	        }
  2733	
  2734	        let normalized = trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase();
  2735	        Ok(match normalized.as_str() {
  2736	            "cli" => SessionSource::Cli,
  2737	            "vscode" => SessionSource::VSCode,
  2738	            "exec" => SessionSource::Exec,
  2739	            "mcp" | "appserver" | "app-server" | "app_server" => SessionSource::Mcp,
  2740	            "unknown" => SessionSource::Unknown,
  2741	            _ => SessionSource::Custom(normalized),
  2742	        })
  2743	    }

  2786	            SessionSource::Cli

  2792	        }
  2793	    }

  2795	    pub fn matches_product_restriction(&self, products: &[Product]) -> bool {
  2796	        products.is_empty()
  2797	            || self
  2798	                .restriction_product()
  2799	                .is_some_and(|product| product.matches_product_restriction(products))
  2800	    }

  2866	fn multi_agent_version_from_items(
  2867	    items: &[RolloutItem],
  2868	    thread_id: Option<ThreadId>,
  2869	) -> Option<MultiAgentVersion> {
  2870	    let session_meta_version = items.iter().rev().find_map(|item| match item {
  2871	        RolloutItem::SessionMeta(meta_line)
  2872	            if thread_id.is_none_or(|thread_id| meta_line.meta.id == thread_id) =>
  2873	        {
  2874	            meta_line.meta.multi_agent_version
  2875	        }
  2876	        _ => None,
  2877	    });
  2878	
  2879	    session_meta_version.or_else(|| {
  2880	        items.iter().rev().find_map(|item| match item {
  2881	            RolloutItem::TurnContext(turn_context) => turn_context.multi_agent_version,
  2882	            RolloutItem::SessionMeta(_)
  2883	            | RolloutItem::ResponseItem(_)
  2884	            | RolloutItem::InterAgentCommunication(_)
  2885	            | RolloutItem::Compacted(_)
  2886	            | RolloutItem::EventMsg(_) => None,
  2887	        })
  2888	    })
  2889	}

  2900	/// SessionMeta contains session-level data that doesn't correspond to a specific turn.
  2901	///
  2902	/// NOTE: There used to be an `instructions` field here, which stored user_instructions, but we
  2903	/// now save that on TurnContext. base_instructions stores the base instructions for the session,
  2904	/// and should be used when there is no config override.
  2905	#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, JsonSchema, TS)]
  2906	pub struct SessionMeta {
  2907	    pub id: ThreadId,
  2908	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  2909	    pub forked_from_id: Option<ThreadId>,
  2910	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  2911	    pub parent_thread_id: Option<ThreadId>,
  2912	    pub timestamp: String,
  2913	    pub cwd: PathBuf,
  2914	    pub originator: String,
  2915	    pub cli_version: String,
  2916	    #[serde(default)]
  2917	    pub source: SessionSource,
  2918	    /// Optional analytics source classification for this thread.
  2919	    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  2920	    pub thread_source: Option<ThreadSource>,
  2921	    /// Optional random unique nickname assigned to an AgentControl-spawned sub-agent.
  2922	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  2923	    pub agent_nickname: Option<String>,
  2924	    /// Optional role (agent_role) assigned to an AgentControl-spawned sub-agent.
  2925	    #[serde(default, alias = "agent_type", skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  2926	    pub agent_role: Option<String>,
  2927	    /// Optional canonical agent path assigned to an AgentControl-spawned sub-agent.
  2928	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  2929	    pub agent_path: Option<String>,
  2930	    pub model_provider: Option<String>,
  2931	    /// base_instructions for the session. This *should* always be present when creating a new session,
  2932	    /// but may be missing for older sessions. If not present, fall back to rendering the base_instructions
  2933	    /// from ModelsManager.
  2934	    pub base_instructions: Option<BaseInstructions>,
  2935	    #[serde(

  2938	        skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"
  2939	    )]
  2940	    pub dynamic_tools: Option<Vec<DynamicToolSpec>>,
  2941	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  2942	    pub memory_mode: Option<String>,
  2943	    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  2944	    pub multi_agent_version: Option<MultiAgentVersion>,
  2945	}

codex
Upstream does persist subagent relationships in two places: `session_meta.source.subagent.thread_spawn.parent_thread_id` and `event_msg.collab_agent_spawn_end.new_thread_id`. That means the 0/72 `child_session_id` result is not “by source design”; it is either resolver/store/UI failure or an adapter-store contract gap.

    64	// classifySource resolves the polymorphic source enum into a canonical
    65	// sourceKind and, for a sub-agent thread_spawn, the parent ThreadId (else "").
    66	// Tolerates every shape in adapter-codex.md:114-122 and never panics on an
    67	// unknown object — it returns sourceOther so the line is still ingested.
    68	func (p *sessionMetaPayload) classifySource() (sourceKind, string) {
    69		body := bytes.TrimSpace(p.Source)
    70		if len(body) == 0 || bytes.Equal(body, []byte("null")) {
    71			return sourceRoot, ""
    72		}
    73		// Bare string form: "cli" | "exec" | "vscode" | "mcp" | "unknown".
    74		var s string
    75		if json.Unmarshal(body, &s) == nil {
    76			if k, ok := stringSourceKinds[s]; ok {
    77				return k, ""
    78			}
    79			return sourceOther, ""
    80		}
    81		// Object form: exactly one of custom / internal / subagent / other.
    82		var obj struct {
    83			Custom   json.RawMessage `json:"custom"`
    84			Internal json.RawMessage `json:"internal"`
    85			Subagent json.RawMessage `json:"subagent"`
    86		}
    87		if json.Unmarshal(body, &obj) != nil {
    88			return sourceOther, ""
    89		}
    90		switch {
    91		case len(obj.Custom) > 0:
    92			return sourceRoot, ""
    93		case len(obj.Internal) > 0:
    94			return sourceInternal, ""
    95		case len(obj.Subagent) > 0:
    96			return sourceSubagent, parentFromSubagent(obj.Subagent)
    97		default:
    98			return sourceOther, ""
    99		}
   100	}

     9	// This file handles the codex sub-agent collab lifecycle event_msgs (F3): the
    10	// parent→child spawn link (collab_agent_spawn_end) and the recognized-but-op-less
    11	// markers (collab_close_end / collab_waiting_end, dispatched in ops_event.go).
    12	// Kept separate from ops_enrich.go so the enrichment path stays focused.
    13	
    14	// mapCollabSpawn handles event_msg.collab_agent_spawn_end (spec "Sub-Agent
    15	// Linkage", F3). It emits a session op (Kind=session, Name=spawn) whose
    16	// ChildSessionNativeID is the spawned thread's new_thread_id, so the topology
    17	// view links the parent rollout to the child sub-agent rollout. The real wire
    18	// link is sender_thread_id→new_thread_id (NOT agent_ref.thread_id, which the
    19	// earlier spec wrongly named). The child rollout lands as its own file with
    20	// source.subagent.thread_spawn.parent_thread_id; the ingester relaxes the FK and
    21	// re-links when the child arrives (canonical-events.md out-of-order child). The
    22	// spawn metadata (nickname/role/model) goes into the op Extras for the UI. When
    23	// new_thread_id is absent the op is suppressed and a DBG log keeps it visible.
    24	func (m *fileMapper) mapCollabSpawn(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64) []canonical.Event {
    25		sp := decodeCollabSpawn(rec.Raw)
    26		if sp.newThreadID == "" {
    27			return []canonical.Event{m.logEntry(advance(tsUs), "DBG", "collab_agent_spawn_end_no_child", nil)}
    28		}
    29		ts := m.ensureTurn(tsUs)
    30		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 3)
    31		if ev := m.emitTurnStarted(ts, advance(tsUs)); ev != nil {
    32			out = append(out, ev)
    33		}
    34		turnSeq, opSeq := m.nextOp(ts)
    35		extras := collabSpawnExtras(sp)
    36		out = append(out,
    37			canonical.OpStartedEvent{
    38				EventBase:            advance(tsUs),
    39				SessionNativeID:      m.nativeID,
    40				TurnSeq:              turnSeq,
    41				Seq:                  opSeq,
    42				ParentOpSeq:          -1,
    43				Kind:                 canonical.OpSession,
    44				Name:                 "spawn",
    45				ChildSessionNativeID: sp.newThreadID,
    46				Extras:               extras,
    47			},
    48			canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{
    49				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
    50				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
    51				TurnSeq:         turnSeq,
    52				Seq:             opSeq,
    53				Status:          spawnStatus(sp.status),
    54				EndTs:           tsUs,
    55			},
    56		)
    57		return out
    58	}

    60	// collabSpawn is the decoded subset of a collab_agent_spawn_end payload (F3).
    61	// Field names match the real wire form (5 real files; keys sender_thread_id,
    62	// new_thread_id, new_agent_nickname, new_agent_role, model, reasoning_effort,
    63	// status).
    64	type collabSpawn struct {
    65		senderThreadID  string
    66		newThreadID     string
    67		newAgentNick    string
    68		newAgentRole    string
    69		model           string
    70		reasoningEffort string
    71		status          string
    72	}
    73	
    74	// decodeCollabSpawn reads the collab_agent_spawn_end payload fields off the
    75	// verbatim envelope (F3). Unknown siblings are dropped (forward-compat).
    76	func decodeCollabSpawn(raw []byte) collabSpawn {
    77		var env struct {
    78			Payload struct {
    79				SenderThreadID  string `json:"sender_thread_id"`
    80				NewThreadID     string `json:"new_thread_id"`
    81				NewAgentNick    string `json:"new_agent_nickname"`
    82				NewAgentRole    string `json:"new_agent_role"`
    83				Model           string `json:"model"`
    84				ReasoningEffort string `json:"reasoning_effort"`
    85				Status          string `json:"status"`
    86			} `json:"payload"`
    87		}
    88		if json.Unmarshal(raw, &env) != nil {
    89			return collabSpawn{}
    90		}
    91		p := env.Payload
    92		return collabSpawn{
    93			senderThreadID:  p.SenderThreadID,
    94			newThreadID:     p.NewThreadID,
    95			newAgentNick:    p.NewAgentNick,
    96			newAgentRole:    p.NewAgentRole,
    97			model:           p.Model,
    98			reasoningEffort: p.ReasoningEffort,
    99			status:          p.Status,
   100		}
   101	}
   102	
   103	// collabSpawnExtras builds the spawn op's Extras from the decoded fields (F3),
   104	// surfacing the spawned agent's nickname/role/model and the relationship marker
   105	// so the UI can label the sub-agent edge. Returns a non-empty map (the relation
   106	// is always set when a child exists).
   107	func collabSpawnExtras(sp collabSpawn) map[string]any {
   108		extras := map[string]any{"relationship": "sub_agent"}
   109		if sp.senderThreadID != "" {
   110			extras["sender_thread_id"] = sp.senderThreadID
   111		}
   112		if sp.newAgentNick != "" {
   113			extras["new_agent_nickname"] = sp.newAgentNick
   114		}
   115		if sp.newAgentRole != "" {
   116			extras["new_agent_role"] = sp.newAgentRole
   117		}
   118		if sp.model != "" {
   119			extras["model"] = sp.model
   120		}
   121		if sp.reasoningEffort != "" {
   122			extras["reasoning_effort"] = sp.reasoningEffort
   123		}
   124		return extras
   125	}
   126	
   127	// spawnStatus maps a collab_agent_spawn_end.status to a canonical op status: a
   128	// "failed"/"error" reported status is failed; anything else (including the
   129	// common "completed"/"") is completed (F3).
   130	func spawnStatus(status string) string {
   131		switch status {
   132		case "failed", "error":
   133			return "failed"
   134		default:
   135			return "completed"
   136		}
   137	}

   982	// resolveOpStartedChild looks up the child session row (when the event names
   983	// one) and either returns its id directly OR stashes the child native id
   984	// into the op's extras_json.aiViewer.childNativeId so the resolver can re-link
   985	// it once the child session lands (P1a). A SQL error other than ErrNoRows is
   986	// propagated unchanged. When the event carries no ChildSessionNativeID, the
   987	// child link stays NULL and the extras blob is the event's untouched extras.
   988	func (w *writer) resolveOpStartedChild(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, ev canonical.OpStartedEvent) (sql.NullString, map[string]any, error) {
   989		if ev.ChildSessionNativeID == "" {
   990			return sql.NullString{}, ev.Extras, nil
   991		}
   992		cid, err := w.lookupSessionID(ctx, tx, ev.ChildSessionNativeID)
   993		if err == nil {
   994			return sql.NullString{String: cid, Valid: true}, ev.Extras, nil
   995		}
   996		if !errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
   997			return sql.NullString{}, nil, err
   998		}
   999		// Child has not landed yet (parent transcript is read before, or in a
  1000		// different batch than, the child sidechain) — leave the link NULL and
  1001		// stash the child native id in ops.extras_json.aiViewer.childNativeId.
  1002		// The resolver re-links child_session_id from that stash once the child
  1003		// session lands (P1a) — mirroring the session aiViewer.parentNativeId
  1004		// stash + resolver pass.
  1005		stashed := mergeExtras(ev.Extras, map[string]any{
  1006			"aiViewer": map[string]any{"childNativeId": ev.ChildSessionNativeID},
  1007		})
  1008		return sql.NullString{}, stashed, nil
  1009	}

   227	// linkOpChildren re-links ops.child_session_id from the child native id stashed
   228	// in ops.extras_json.aiViewer.childNativeId once the referenced child session
   229	// lands (P1a). The parent Agent op is written before its child sidechain
   230	// session exists, so child_session_id starts NULL and the native id is stashed;
   231	// without this pass the parent op would permanently show no child (the
   232	// session-only linkParents/linkRoots passes never touch ops). It records the
   233	// op's OWNING session id — the PARENT session — into affected so an open
   234	// parent-detail view refetches and renders the now-linked child op
   235	// (sse-protocol.md §session_changed). The child session is matched on
   236	// (source_id, native_id); source_id is resolved by joining through the op's
   237	// session row since ops carry no source_id column. modernc.org/sqlite supports
   238	// UPDATE … FROM and UPDATE … RETURNING.
   239	func (r *resolver) linkOpChildren(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, affected map[string]struct{}) error {
   240		before := len(affected)
   241		rows, err := tx.QueryContext(ctx, `
   242	UPDATE ops SET child_session_id = (
   243	    SELECT c.id FROM sessions c
   244	     JOIN sessions parent ON parent.id = ops.session_id
   245	     WHERE c.source_id = parent.source_id
   246	       AND c.native_id = json_extract(ops.extras_json, '$.aiViewer.childNativeId')
   247	)
   248	WHERE ops.child_session_id IS NULL
   249	  AND json_extract(ops.extras_json, '$.aiViewer.childNativeId') IS NOT NULL
   250	  AND json_extract(ops.extras_json, '$.aiViewer.childNativeId') <> ''
   251	  AND EXISTS (
   252	      SELECT 1 FROM sessions c
   253	       JOIN sessions parent ON parent.id = ops.session_id
   254	       WHERE c.source_id = parent.source_id
   255	         AND c.native_id = json_extract(ops.extras_json, '$.aiViewer.childNativeId')
   256	  )
   257	RETURNING session_id
   258	`)
   259		if err != nil {
   260			return fmt.Errorf("resolver UPDATE op child: %w", err)
   261		}
   262		if err := scanLinkedRows(rows, affected); err != nil {
   263			return fmt.Errorf("resolver UPDATE op child: %w", err)
   264		}
   265		if r.logger != nil && len(affected) > before {
   266			r.logger.Debug("resolver: linked orphan op children", "affected", len(affected)-before)
   267		}
   268		return nil
   269	}

    10	// payloadLocationURI builds a containment-checked "file://<resolved-abs>"
    11	// location for a body inline in a rollout file (spec rule #6/#7/#8, edge #7:
    12	// large bodies are referenced, never inlined). The path is resolved with
    13	// filepath.EvalSymlinks and verified to stay inside the configured sessions
    14	// root before it is surfaced (security.md §6 "No symlink traversal escape").
    15	// Returns ("", err) when the path escapes the root so the caller can fall back
    16	// to the cleaned absolute path rather than emit a lossy ref. When root is empty
    17	// (mapper-only unit tests) the check is skipped and the cleaned absolute path is
    18	// returned. Mirrors claude_code/payloads.go verbatim; the only codex difference
    19	// is that withinResolvedRoot + evalSymlinksAllowingTail already live in
    20	// stream.go (the scanner reuses them), so this file re-adds only the per-call
    21	// resolveWithinRoot wrapper Chunk C noted it had dropped.
    22	func payloadLocationURI(root, abs string) (string, error) {
    23		cleaned := filepath.Clean(abs)
    24		if root == "" {
    25			return "file://" + filepath.ToSlash(cleaned), nil
    26		}
    27		resolved, ok, err := resolveWithinRoot(root, cleaned)
    28		if err != nil {
    29			return "", err
    30		}
    31		if !ok {
    32			return "", fmt.Errorf("payload path escapes root: %q", abs)
    33		}
    34		return "file://" + filepath.ToSlash(resolved), nil
    35	}
    36	
    37	// resolveWithinRoot resolves both root AND abs through filepath.EvalSymlinks and
    38	// reports whether the fully-resolved path stays inside the fully-resolved root
    39	// (security.md §6 "No symlink traversal escape"). It resolves the root every
    40	// call, so per-file walk callers that share one root resolve it once and use
    41	// withinResolvedRoot (stream.go) instead — this single-shot wrapper is for the
    42	// mapper's payload-URI builder, which is handed only the absolute file path. A
    43	// legitimately symlinked sessions root (e.g. ~/.codex → an external volume)
    44	// still works: containment is judged against the RESOLVED root. A symlink inside
    45	// the tree that points outside the resolved root is refused (ok=false). Returns:
    46	//   - (resolvedAbs, true, nil)  — abs resolves to a path under the root.
    47	//   - ("", false, nil)          — abs resolves outside the root (escape).
    48	//   - ("", false, err)          — the path or root could not be resolved.
    49	//
    50	// When abs does not yet exist on disk, the deepest existing ancestor is resolved
    51	// and the non-existent tail re-appended, so a not-yet-created file is judged by
    52	// where it WOULD live (a non-existent path cannot itself be a symlink to
    53	// elsewhere). Mirrors claude_code/payloads.go's resolveWithinRoot.
    54	func resolveWithinRoot(root, abs string) (string, bool, error) {
    55		resolvedRoot, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(filepath.Clean(root))
    56		if err != nil {
    57			return "", false, fmt.Errorf("resolve root %q: %w", root, err)
    58		}
    59		return withinResolvedRoot(resolvedRoot, abs)
    60	}
    61	
    62	// payloadURI builds the PayloadRef LocationURI for a body inline in this
    63	// rollout file at the given 1-based line number (spec rule #6/#7/#8, edge #7).
    64	// The form is "file://<symlink-resolved-abs>#L<line>" so the presenter reads the
    65	// exact record on demand without ai-viewer ever copying the body into SQLite.
    66	//
    67	// Containment (Chunk D, security.md §6): the absolute path is resolved through
    68	// symlinks and verified to stay inside the configured sessions root via
    69	// payloadLocationURI. The "#L<line>" anchor is appended AFTER the file:// path is
    70	// built so the anchor is identical to Chunk B's contract
    71	// (TestMapper_PayloadRefLineAnchor). When m.root is empty (mapper-only tests) the
    72	// containment resolve is skipped and the cleaned absolute path is used; when
    73	// m.absPath is empty the URI is just the line anchor.
    74	//
    75	// The scanner is the authoritative containment gate: readRollout (scanner.go)
    76	// refuses any file that resolves outside the root BEFORE a single line is
    77	// streamed, so by the time the mapper builds a ref the owning file is already
    78	// known to be contained. A resolve failure or apparent escape here (e.g. the
    79	// file removed between the scanner's open and this build — impossible while the
    80	// scanner holds the fd, but handled defensively) therefore falls back to the
    81	// cleaned absolute path rather than dropping the anchor, keeping the ref usable
    82	// and the op→payload linkage (payload_refs.op_id NOT NULL) intact.
    83	func (m *fileMapper) payloadURI(lineNo int) string {
    84		anchor := ""
    85		if lineNo > 0 {
    86			anchor = fmt.Sprintf("#L%d", lineNo)
    87		}
    88		if m.absPath == "" {
    89			return anchor
    90		}
    91		uri, err := payloadLocationURI(m.root, m.absPath)
    92		if err != nil {
    93			// Containment resolve failed (escape or unresolvable). The scanner
    94			// already vetted the file before streaming, so fall back to the cleaned
    95			// absolute path rather than emit a lossy ref.
    96			uri = "file://" + filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(m.absPath))
    97		}
    98		return uri + anchor
    99	}
   100	
   101	// payloadRef builds a PayloadRefEvent for a body inline in this rollout at the
   102	// record currently being mapped (m.lineNo). It is scoped to the owning op
   103	// (turnSeq/opSeq) so it references an op that EXISTS — payload_refs.op_id is NOT
   104	// NULL REFERENCES ops(id), so an orphan ref would FK-roll-back the ingest batch
   105	// (mirrors claude_code's P1.1a discipline). OriginalBytes is the byte length of
   106	// the verbatim line so the presenter can budget a read; -1 when unknown.
   107	func (m *fileMapper) payloadRef(base canonical.EventBase, turnSeq, opSeq int, kind, format string, originalBytes int64) canonical.PayloadRefEvent {
   108		return canonical.PayloadRefEvent{
   109			EventBase:       base,
   110			SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   111			TurnSeq:         turnSeq,
   112			OpSeq:           opSeq,
   113			PayloadKind:     kind,
   114			Format:          format,
   115			LocationURI:     m.payloadURI(m.lineNo),
   116			OriginalBytes:   originalBytes,
   117		}
   118	}

    97	// parseLine decodes one JSONL line into a record. Whitespace-only / empty lines
    98	// return (record{}, true, nil) to signal "skip silently". Malformed JSON or a
    99	// missing top-level type returns a wrapped error. An unknown top-level type
   100	// returns errUnknownRecordType (wrapped); an unknown nested payload.type returns
   101	// errUnknownPayloadType (wrapped). A catch-all/no-op nested variant (e.g.
   102	// ghost_snapshot) or an absent payload/nested-type returns (record, true, nil).
   103	func parseLine(line []byte) (record, bool, error) {
   104		trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(line)
   105		if len(trimmed) == 0 {
   106			return record{}, true, nil
   107		}
   108	
   109		var env envelope
   110		if err := json.Unmarshal(trimmed, &env); err != nil {
   111			return record{}, false, fmt.Errorf("decode envelope: %w", err)
   112		}
   113		if env.Type == "" {
   114			return record{}, false, errors.New("record.type is required")
   115		}
   116	
   117		rec := record{Env: env, Raw: append([]byte(nil), trimmed...)}
   118		switch env.Type {
   119		case recSessionMeta:
   120			var p sessionMetaPayload
   121			if err := decodePayload(env.Payload, &p); err != nil {
   122				return record{}, false, fmt.Errorf("decode session_meta: %w", err)
   123			}
   124			rec.SessionMeta = &p
   125		case recTurnContext:
   126			var p turnContextPayload
   127			if err := decodePayload(env.Payload, &p); err != nil {
   128				return record{}, false, fmt.Errorf("decode turn_context: %w", err)
   129			}
   130			rec.TurnContext = &p
   131		case recResponseItem:
   132			return decodeResponseItem(rec)
   133		case recEventMsg:
   134			return decodeEventMsg(rec)
   135		case recCompacted:
   136			var p compactedPayload
   137			if err := decodePayload(env.Payload, &p); err != nil {
   138				return record{}, false, fmt.Errorf("decode compacted: %w", err)
   139			}
   140			rec.Compacted = &p
   141		default:
   142			return record{}, false, &unknownTypeError{Type: string(env.Type)}
   143		}
   144		return rec, false, nil
   145	}
   146	
   147	// decodePayload unmarshals a payload body into dst, tolerating an absent body
   148	// (a known top-level type with no payload is not an error — it just carries no
   149	// nested data). A bare JSON null is likewise treated as absent.
   150	func decodePayload(payload json.RawMessage, dst any) error {
   151		body := bytes.TrimSpace(payload)
   152		if len(body) == 0 || bytes.Equal(body, []byte("null")) {
   153			return nil
   154		}
   155		return json.Unmarshal(body, dst)
   156	}
   157	
   158	// nestedType extracts only the nested payload.type discriminator without
   159	// committing to a full typed decode. Returns "" when the payload is absent or
   160	// carries no type (both tolerated by the callers).
   161	func nestedType(payload json.RawMessage) (string, error) {
   162		body := bytes.TrimSpace(payload)
   163		if len(body) == 0 || bytes.Equal(body, []byte("null")) {
   164			return "", nil
   165		}
   166		var probe struct {
   167			Type string `json:"type"`
   168		}
   169		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &probe); err != nil {
   170			return "", err
   171		}
   172		return probe.Type, nil
   173	}
   174	
   175	// decodeResponseItem handles the response_item top-level type: it reads the
   176	// nested discriminator, classifies it (known / catch-all-no-op / unknown), and
   177	// only fully decodes the known variants. Unknown nested types surface
   178	// errUnknownPayloadType; catch-all variants (ResponseItem::Other upstream, e.g.
   179	// ghost_snapshot) skip silently per rule #21.
   180	func decodeResponseItem(rec record) (record, bool, error) {
   181		nt, err := nestedType(rec.Env.Payload)
   182		if err != nil {
   183			return record{}, false, fmt.Errorf("decode response_item payload type: %w", err)
   184		}
   185		if nt == "" {
   186			return rec, true, nil
   187		}
   188		if _, ok := responseItemNoOp[nt]; ok {
   189			return rec, true, nil
   190		}
   191		if _, ok := responseItemTypes[nt]; !ok {
   192			return record{}, false, &unknownPayloadTypeError{Owner: string(recResponseItem), Type: nt}
   193		}
   194		var p responseItemPayload
   195		if err := decodePayload(rec.Env.Payload, &p); err != nil {
   196			return record{}, false, fmt.Errorf("decode response_item: %w", err)
   197		}
   198		rec.ResponseItem = &p
   199		return rec, false, nil
   200	}
   201	
   202	// decodeEventMsg handles the event_msg top-level type, mirroring
   203	// decodeResponseItem: known nested types decode; catch-all/no-op variants skip
   204	// silently; unknown nested types surface errUnknownPayloadType.
   205	func decodeEventMsg(rec record) (record, bool, error) {
   206		nt, err := nestedType(rec.Env.Payload)
   207		if err != nil {
   208			return record{}, false, fmt.Errorf("decode event_msg payload type: %w", err)
   209		}
   210		if nt == "" {
   211			return rec, true, nil
   212		}
   213		if _, ok := eventMsgNoOp[nt]; ok {
   214			return rec, true, nil
   215		}
   216		if _, ok := eventMsgTypes[nt]; !ok {
   217			return record{}, false, &unknownPayloadTypeError{Owner: string(recEventMsg), Type: nt}
   218		}
   219		var p eventMsgPayload
   220		if err := decodePayload(rec.Env.Payload, &p); err != nil {
   221			return record{}, false, fmt.Errorf("decode event_msg: %w", err)
   222		}
   223		rec.EventMsg = &p
   224		return rec, false, nil
   225	}

    16	// mapTurnContext handles a turn_context record (spec rule #2). It opens (or
    17	// re-activates) the turn for turn_id, emits TurnStartedEvent the first time the
    18	// turn is seen (idempotent with task_started), emits SessionUpdatedEvent(Model)
    19	// the first time a model is learned, and snapshots the sandbox/effort/approval
    20	// policy into the turn's extras (spec gap #3). A turn_context after mid-turn
    21	// compaction re-activates the same turn_id without re-emitting TurnStarted.
    22	func (m *fileMapper) mapTurnContext(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase) []canonical.Event {
    23		p := rec.TurnContext
    24		if p == nil {
    25			return nil
    26		}
    27		tsUs := m.recordTs(rec)
    28		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 3)
    29		// A new turn_id opening supersedes the prior open turn (F1/F2, spec edge #2/#3).
    30		// supersedePriorTurn decides the prior turn's close status from ITS OWN format
    31		// (NEW-format → failed/replaced; OLD-format → completed) and is a no-op for a
    32		// re-activating turn_context with the SAME turn_id (post-compaction).
    33		out = append(out, m.supersedePriorTurn(p.TurnID, advance, tsUs)...)
    34		ts := m.openTurn(p.TurnID, tsUs)
    35		if ev := m.emitTurnStarted(ts, advance(tsUs)); ev != nil {
    36			out = append(out, ev)
    37		}
    38		// Snapshot per-turn policy (spec rule #2, gap #3).
    39		if sb := p.sandboxType(); sb != "" {
    40			ts.sandbox = sb
    41		}
    42		if p.Effort != "" {
    43			ts.effort = p.Effort
    44		}
    45		if p.ApprovalPolicy != "" {
    46			ts.approvalPolicy = p.ApprovalPolicy
    47		}
    48		// Learn the model and announce it once (spec rule #2). The active turn
    49		// always uses the latest model so later ops are stamped correctly.
    50		if p.Model != "" {
    51			m.model = p.Model
    52			if !m.modelSeen {
    53				m.modelSeen = true
    54				out = append(out, canonical.SessionUpdatedEvent{
    55					EventBase: advance(tsUs),
    56					NativeID:  m.nativeID,
    57					Model:     p.Model,
    58				})
    59			}
    60		}
    61		return out
    62	}
    63	
    64	// mapCompacted handles a top-level compacted line (spec rule #20). It emits a
    65	// single compaction op (Kind=compaction, Name=compaction) with the
    66	// replacement_history size and a message preview in Extras; the full summary
    67	// body goes to a PayloadRef. This is the data-bearing representation; the
    68	// adjacent event_msg.context_compacted bare marker (same timestamp) is its
    69	// companion and is SUPPRESSED so ONE op is emitted per compaction (F5, spec rule
    70	// #20). recordIdx-1 is the current record's index (mapRecord pre-incremented
    71	// recordIdx); recording it lets the immediately-following context_compacted
    72	// recognize itself as the companion.
    73	func (m *fileMapper) mapCompacted(rec record, advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase) []canonical.Event {
    74		p := rec.Compacted
    75		tsUs := m.recordTs(rec)
    76		extras := map[string]any{"trigger": "auto"}
    77		if p != nil {
    78			extras["replacement_history_size"] = p.replacementHistorySize()
    79			if prev := trimPreview(p.Message, previewMax); prev != "" {
    80				extras["message_preview"] = prev
    81			}
    82		}
    83		// recordIdx was pre-incremented in mapRecord, so recordIdx-1 is THIS line's
    84		// index; recording it lets the immediately-following context_compacted detect
    85		// adjacency (F5). recordIdx is always >= 1 here (this record was counted).
    86		m.compactedSeen = true
    87		m.compactedRecordIdx = m.recordIdx - 1
    88		return m.emitCompactionOp(advance, tsUs, extras, "json")
    89	}
    90	
    91	// suppressContextCompacted reports whether an event_msg.context_compacted record
    92	// is the bare companion marker of the immediately-preceding top-level `compacted`
    93	// line and must NOT emit a second compaction op (F5). The real wire pair is two
    94	// adjacent lines (compacted then context_compacted) with identical timestamps;
    95	// only the data-bearing `compacted` produces the op. A context_compacted with no
    96	// preceding compacted (defensive) is NOT suppressed and emits the op itself.
    97	// recordIdx-1 is the current record's index; the companion is suppressed when the
    98	// recorded `compacted` index is exactly one before it (adjacent).
    99	func (m *fileMapper) suppressContextCompacted() bool {
   100		// recordIdx-1 is THIS context_compacted's index; it is the companion when the
   101		// recorded `compacted` index is exactly one before it (adjacent). recordIdx is
   102		// >= 2 here (a session_meta/turn at minimum precedes any compaction pair), so
   103		// recordIdx-2 does not underflow.
   104		return m.compactedSeen && m.compactedRecordIdx+1 == m.recordIdx-1
   105	}
   106	
   107	// emitCompactionOp emits the OpStarted+OpFinalized compaction pair plus a
   108	// PayloadRef for the summary body (spec rule #20, gap #4). It opens a turn 0
   109	// fallback when compaction precedes any turn_context so the op attaches to a
   110	// real turn row. format is the PayloadRef Format ("json" for a structured
   111	// compaction body). The op carries no tokens; preTokens/postTokens are unknown
   112	// for codex (the rollout records only the summary), so trigger is the only
   113	// scalar.
   114	func (m *fileMapper) emitCompactionOp(advance func(int64) canonical.EventBase, tsUs int64, extras map[string]any, format string) []canonical.Event {
   115		ts := m.ensureTurn(tsUs)
   116		out := make([]canonical.Event, 0, 3)
   117		if ev := m.emitTurnStarted(ts, advance(tsUs)); ev != nil {
   118			out = append(out, ev)
   119		}
   120		ts.opSeq++
   121		opSeq := ts.opSeq
   122		out = append(out,
   123			canonical.OpStartedEvent{
   124				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   125				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   126				TurnSeq:         ts.seq,
   127				Seq:             opSeq,
   128				ParentOpSeq:     -1,
   129				Kind:            canonical.OpCompaction,
   130				Name:            "compaction",
   131				Extras:          extras,
   132			},
   133			canonical.OpFinalizedEvent{
   134				EventBase:       advance(tsUs),
   135				SessionNativeID: m.nativeID,
   136				TurnSeq:         ts.seq,
   137				Seq:             opSeq,
   138				Status:          "completed",
   139				EndTs:           tsUs,
   140			},
   141			m.payloadRef(advance(tsUs), ts.seq, opSeq, "log", format, -1),
   142		)
   143		return out
   144	}
   145	
   146	// ensureTurn returns the active turn, opening a fallback turn (under the active
   147	// turn_id, or the absent-turn_id bucket "") when no turn is open yet. Used by
   148	// ops that can legitimately precede a turn boundary (compaction, a stray
   149	// message in an old-CLI rollout — spec edge #3).
   150	func (m *fileMapper) ensureTurn(tsUs int64) *turnState {
   151		if m.haveActiveTurn {
   152			if ts, ok := m.turns[m.activeTurnID]; ok {
   153				return ts
   154			}
   155		}
   156		return m.openTurn("", tsUs)
   157	}

   159	// nextOp allocates the next op Seq in the turn and returns (turnSeq, opSeq).
   160	func (m *fileMapper) nextOp(ts *turnState) (int, int) {
   161		ts.opSeq++
   162		return ts.seq, ts.opSeq
   163	}

   165	// trackOp records an in-flight op by call_id so its matching *_output (or an

   171	func (m *fileMapper) trackOp(callID, turnID string, turnSeq, opSeq int, name, namespace string) {

    10	// execDuration is the Rust std::time::Duration wire shape codex serializes for
    11	// exec_command_end.duration: ALWAYS the {secs,nanos} object (real corpus: 20000/
    12	// 20000 exec_command_end lines, keys always nanos,secs — never a bare number or

    20	// millis normalizes the {secs,nanos} duration to integer milliseconds (spec rule
    21	// #14 exec_duration_ms). Returns -1 when the field was absent (both zero is a
    22	// legitimately sub-millisecond command, so 0 is a real value, not "missing").
    23	func (d *execDuration) millis(present bool) int64 {
    24		if !present {
    25			return -1
    26		}
    27		return d.Secs*1000 + d.Nanos/1_000_000
    28	}

    30	// execCommandExtras extracts the exec_command_end telemetry merged into the op
    31	// (spec rule #14): exit_code, duration (normalized to exec_duration_ms), cwd,

    35	func execCommandExtras(raw []byte) map[string]any {

    46			return nil
    47		}

    70	// webSearchExtras extracts event_msg.web_search_end query + action (spec rule
    71	// #11). The end event's `action` is ALWAYS an object discriminated by `type`
    72	// (real corpus: search | open_page | find_in_page | other); webSearchAction
    73	// reduces it to a compact map carrying the type plus the variant's url / query /
    74	// pattern (G4). Returns nil only when neither a query nor an action is present.
    75	func webSearchExtras(raw []byte) map[string]any {
    76		var env struct {
    77			Payload struct {
    78				Query  string          `json:"query"`
    79				Action json.RawMessage `json:"action"`
    80			} `json:"payload"`
    81		}

    83			return nil

    88		}

    91		}

    94		}

    96	}

    98	// webSearchAction reduces web_search_end.action to a compact Extras map (G4, spec
    99	// rule #11). The action is an object discriminated by `type`; only the
   100	// type-relevant scalar fields are surfaced (url for open_page; query for search;
   101	// pattern + optional url for find_in_page). The queries[] array is dropped (the
   102	// scalar `query` already carries the primary term) so the Extras stays compact.
   103	// Returns nil when the action is absent or carries no type.
   104	func webSearchAction(raw json.RawMessage) map[string]any {
   105		body := jsonTrim(raw)
   106		if len(body) == 0 {
   107			return nil
   108		}
   109		var a struct {
   110			Type    string `json:"type"`
   111			URL     string `json:"url"`
   112			Query   string `json:"query"`
   113			Pattern string `json:"pattern"`
   114		}
   115		if json.Unmarshal(body, &a) != nil || a.Type == "" {
   116			return nil
   117		}
   118		out := map[string]any{"type": a.Type}
   119		if a.URL != "" {
   120			out["url"] = trimPreview(a.URL, previewMax)
   121		}
   122		if a.Query != "" {
   123			out["query"] = trimPreview(a.Query, previewMax)
   124		}
   125		if a.Pattern != "" {
   126			out["pattern"] = trimPreview(a.Pattern, previewMax)
   127		}
   128		return out
   129	}

   134	// ("", "") when the event carries no exit_code (status left to the *_output).
   135	func enrichStatus(raw []byte) (status, errClass string) {
   136		var env struct {

   106		// deterministic, stable-across-rescans per-event identifier. v3 packs a
   107		// monotonic-per-file sequence; v2 is a content hash (not monotonic). It

   110		// a SQL-layer guarantee. See the SourceSeq field doc on EventBase and

   112		EventSourceSeq() uint64
   113		// EventTs returns the event timestamp in UNIX-microseconds (UTC).
   114		EventTs() int64
   115	}

ID: T2-codex-1  
Invariant: 2 USER PROMPTS  
Severity: P0  
Description: Codex user prompts are captured, but as `kind='internal'`, `name='user_input'`, not as canonical `user_input` ops. `OpInternal` is documented as adapter housekeeping that the UI hides by default, so real user prompts can disappear from normal review surfaces. The payload is also labeled `tool_request`, which pollutes tool-request counts. Live DB check: all 24,149 codex `internal` ops are `user_input`, and all 24,149 extra `tool_request` refs are attached to those internal ops.  
Evidence: [internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:119), [internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:160), [internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:171), [internal/canonical/events.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/canonical/events.go:84)  
Proposed invariant:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM ops o
JOIN sessions sess ON sess.id=o.session_id
JOIN sources s ON s.id=sess.source_id
WHERE s.format='codex'
  AND o.name='user_input'
  AND o.kind <> 'user_input';
```
Suggested fix OR accept as known: Fix: add/use a first-class canonical `user_input` op kind or otherwise document and surface `internal/user_input`; change payload kind away from `tool_request`.  
Open questions: Canonical currently has no `OpUserInput`; the spec and schema need an explicit decision.

ID: T6-codex-1

```sql
WITH refs AS (

  WHERE kind='tool_request'
  GROUP BY op_id

SELECT COUNT(*) AS bad_tool_ops

  AND o.kind='tool'

```
Suggested fix OR accept as known: Fix prompt payload classification; invariant should test per-tool-op coverage, not global `tool_request` totals.  
Open questions: None.

ID: T7-codex-1  
Invariant: 7 TOOL RESPONSE PAYLOADS  
Severity: P0  
Description: Codex only attaches `tool_response` payload refs when a `*_output` response item arrives. This explains the response undercount and is real missing payload coverage.

Proposed invariant:
```sql
WITH resp AS (
  SELECT op_id, COUNT(*) c FROM payload_refs
  WHERE kind='tool_response'
  GROUP BY op_id
)
SELECT o.id, o.name, o.tool_namespace
FROM ops o
JOIN sessions sess ON sess.id=o.session_id
JOIN sources s ON s.id=sess.source_id
LEFT JOIN resp r ON r.op_id=o.id
WHERE s.format='codex'
  AND o.kind='tool'
  AND o.status IN ('completed','failed')
  AND COALESCE(r.c,0)=0;
```
Suggested fix OR accept as known: Fix: emit `tool_response` refs for data-bearing `event_msg.*_end` records, or explicitly document which codex tool end-events have no payload body.  
Open questions: Need live per-tool-name breakdown once DB joins are stable; several large joins returned `disk I/O error` in this sandbox.

ID: T5-codex-1  
Invariant: 5 TOOLS  
Severity: P1

If those events are persisted without companion `response_item.function_call` records, dynamic tool invocations are dropped from canonical tool coverage.

```go
// Assert at least one canonical OpTool with request/response payload refs.
```
Suggested fix OR accept as known: Fix if persisted in real rollouts; otherwise document as recognized non-persisted/diagnostic event.  
Open questions: Need corpus count for `payload.type IN ('dynamic_tool_call_request','dynamic_tool_call_response')`.

**Overall Assessment**

The codex adapter is better than the CTO baseline suggested for reasoning and subagent linkage, but it has real canonical accuracy bugs around user prompts and tool response payloads. The largest missed point is that the tool-request overcount is fully explained by `internal/user_input` prompt refs, not duplicate tool refs. The biggest real data-loss risk is response-bearing tool end-events being reduced to extras/finalization without `tool_response` payload refs.

**Things The CTO Missed**

- Codex `session` ops are currently linked in the live DB: 72/72 have `child_session_id`, so the 0/72 baseline is stale or queried incorrectly.
- Reasoning refs belong to `reasoning` ops by adapter design; comparing them to `llm` ops is the wrong invariant for codex.
- `session_meta.parent_thread_id` is present upstream but not decoded by the adapter.
- Dynamic tool event messages are recognized but only logged, which may miss tool calls if no companion response item exists.

Evidence: `/opt/baddisk/monitoring/repos/ai/openai__codex/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs:1337`, `/opt/baddisk/monitoring/repos/ai/openai__codex/codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs:1339`, [internal/adapters/codex/types.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/types.go:239), [internal/adapters/codex/ops_event.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_event.go:84)  
Proposed invariant:
```go
// Fixture with event_msg.dynamic_tool_call_request + response.
// Assert at least one canonical OpTool with request/response payload refs.
```
Suggested fix OR accept as known: Fix if persisted in real rollouts; otherwise document as recognized non-persisted/diagnostic event.  
Open questions: Need corpus count for `payload.type IN ('dynamic_tool_call_request','dynamic_tool_call_response')`.

**Overall Assessment**

The codex adapter is better than the CTO baseline suggested for reasoning and subagent linkage, but it has real canonical accuracy bugs around user prompts and tool response payloads. The largest missed point is that the tool-request overcount is fully explained by `internal/user_input` prompt refs, not duplicate tool refs. The biggest real data-loss risk is response-bearing tool end-events being reduced to extras/finalization without `tool_response` payload refs.

**Things The CTO Missed**

- Codex `session` ops are currently linked in the live DB: 72/72 have `child_session_id`, so the 0/72 baseline is stale or queried incorrectly.
- Reasoning refs belong to `reasoning` ops by adapter design; comparing them to `llm` ops is the wrong invariant for codex.
- `session_meta.parent_thread_id` is present upstream but not decoded by the adapter.
- Dynamic tool event messages are recognized but only logged, which may miss tool calls if no companion response item exists.

- The codex baseline was partly stale/wrong: current DB shows `72/72` codex session ops have `child_session_id`, and reasoning refs map to `reasoning` ops by design.
- Real bugs remain: codex user prompts are misclassified as `internal/user_input`, and that exactly explains the `tool_request` overcount.
- Biggest data-loss risk: some tool end-events may finalize tools without a `tool_response` payload ref.

**Verified Key Findings**

1. `T2-codex-1` P0: codex user prompts are emitted as `kind='internal'`, `name='user_input'`, with payload kind `tool_request`.
   - Evidence: [ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:119), [ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:160), [ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:171)
   - DB check: `internal|user_input|24149`; `tool_request` refs attached to those ops: `24149`
   - Fix direction: add/use a real user-input op representation, or explicitly surface/document this nonstandard mapping.

2. `T6-codex-1` P1: `tool_request` overcount is not duplicate tool refs.
   - Math: `670,183 - 646,034 = 24,149`, exactly the misclassified `internal/user_input` rows.
   - Fix direction: tool-request invariants must be per `ops.kind='tool'`, not raw global counts.

3. `T7-codex-1` P0: tool response refs are incomplete for tools finalized by enrichment end-events.
   - Evidence: [ops_tools.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_tools.go:98), [ops_tools.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_tools.go:107), [ops_enrich.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_enrich.go:217)
   - Caveat: reviewer could not get a stable per-tool DB breakdown due SQLite `disk I/O error` on large joins.
   - Fix direction: emit `tool_response` refs for data-bearing `event_msg.*_end` records where appropriate.

4. `T3-codex-1` P2: reasoning refs are not double-counted against LLM ops.
   - Evidence: [ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:176), [ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:197), [ops_response.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_response.go:209)
   - Current DB aggregate: `reasoning|371517`, matching `llm_reasoning` refs.
   - Fix direction: accept for codex; update invariant wording.

5. `T10-codex-1` P2: current DB refutes `0/72 child_session_id`.
   - Evidence: [ops_collab.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_collab.go:24), [ops_collab.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_collab.go:45)
   - DB check: `72|72`
   - Fix direction: mark old baseline stale or query error.

6. `T10-codex-2` P1: adapter does not decode direct `session_meta.parent_thread_id`.
   - Evidence: [types.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/types.go:49), [types.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/types.go:64)
   - Fix direction: decode `parent_thread_id` as fallback when nested `source.subagent.thread_spawn.parent_thread_id` is absent.

7. `T5-codex-1` P1: dynamic tool call event messages are recognized but may only become debug logs.
   - Evidence: [types.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/types.go:239), [ops_event.go](/home/costa/src/ai-viewer.git/internal/adapters/codex/ops_event.go:84)
   - Fix direction: corpus-check whether these persist without companion `response_item.function_call`; if yes, map them to tool ops.
